children.title: Lipschitz Optimization Goals
children.top_down_role: Distinct global-value, point-location, and solution-set enclosure objectives treated in classical Lipschitz optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Optimal Value Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-value objective for deterministic Lipschitz minimization on a compact feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a compact metric space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous. Globally optimal value search is the task of determining the attained value \[f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] An output \(v\in\mathbb{R}\) solves the task exactly if and only if \(v=f^*\); producing a minimizing point is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Determine the exact minimum value of a Lipschitz function on a compact domain, without necessarily returning a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: global minimum value of the objective

source_refs.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Approximate Value Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-accuracy value objective for deterministic Lipschitz minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous, and fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Globally approximate value search requires an output \(v\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \[|v-f^*|\leq\varepsilon,\qquad f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] If the output must be an evaluated feasible value \(v=f(\widehat x)\), the equivalent one-sided requirement is \(f^*\leq f(\widehat x)\leq f^*+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a value within additive tolerance of the global minimum; for an evaluated feasible point, only the upper error bound is needed.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|v-f^*|\leq\varepsilon\), or \(f^*\leq f(\widehat x)\leq f^*+\varepsilon\) when \(v=f(\widehat x)\).

source_refs.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14

knowledge_statements.title: Single Global Optimizer Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-location objective for deterministic Lipschitz optimization, allowing exact or metric-approximate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty compact metric space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous. Define \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). Exact single-optimizer location asks for any \(\widehat x\in X^*\). Given \(\delta>0\), approximate location asks for \(\widehat x\in X\) satisfying \[\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,X^*):=\inf_{x^*\in X^*}d(\widehat x,x^*)\leq\delta.\] Uniqueness is not required unless a particular optimizer is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return any global minimizer of a Lipschitz objective, or a feasible point within a prescribed metric distance of the optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
For approximate location, \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in X^*\), or \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,X^*)\leq\delta\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: Global Optimizer Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Recovery goals concerning every globally optimal point rather than a single representative.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimizer Set Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or Hausdorff-accurate recovery of the entire argmin set of a Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous, and define \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). Exact optimizer-set identification returns \(S=X^*\). For \(\delta>0\), Hausdorff-approximate identification returns a nonempty compact set \(S\subseteq X\) satisfying \[d_H(S,X^*)\leq\delta,\qquad d_H(A,B):=\max\!\left\{\sup_{a\in A}\operatorname{dist}(a,B),\sup_{b\in B}\operatorname{dist}(b,A)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover the complete global-minimizer set of a Lipschitz objective exactly or within a specified Hausdorff distance.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
For approximate identification, \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=X^*\), or \(d_H(S,X^*)\leq\delta\).

notation.meaning: Hausdorff distance induced by the metric

children.title: Isolated Global Optimizer Localization
children.top_down_role: Localization settings where distinct global optimizers admit separate neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Global Optimizer Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolation and resolution-dependent localization of one global minimizer of a Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous, and define \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). An optimizer \(x^*\in X^*\) is isolated if there exists \(r>0\) such that \[X^*\cap B(x^*,r)=\{x^*\}.\] Given such an \(r\) and a resolution \(\delta>0\), a localization set for \(x^*\) is a set \(C\subseteq X\) satisfying \(x^*\in C\subseteq B(x^*,r)\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(C)\leq\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimizer is isolated when a neighborhood contains no other optimizer; a localization set contains that optimizer, remains inside such a neighborhood, and has bounded diameter.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*\cap B(x^*,r)=\{x^*\}\) and \(x^*\in C\subseteq B(x^*,r)\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(C)\leq\delta\).

notation.meaning: open metric ball centered at the optimizer

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Global Optimizer Enclosure Construction
children.top_down_role: Certified regions retained as containers for globally optimal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimizer Enclosure Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified outer enclosure of every global optimizer using cellwise lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous, and let \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite family of nonempty subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Suppose \(U=f(\bar x)\) for some \(\bar x\in X\), and \(L(C)\leq\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal P\). Then \[E:=\bigcup\{C\in\mathcal P:L(C)\leq U\}\] is a certified outer enclosure satisfying \(X^*\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the covering cells whose certified lower bounds do not exceed an incumbent feasible value; their union is a certified outer enclosure of every global optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
\(\mathcal P\) is a finite cover of \(X\) by nonempty subsets of \(X\).
\(U=f(\bar x)\) for some \(\bar x\in X\).
\(L(C)\leq\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) for each \(C\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*\subseteq E=\bigcup\{C\in\mathcal P:L(C)\leq U\}\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on a cell

children.title: Nonisolated Optimizer Enclosures
children.top_down_role: Enclosure requirements for continua, plateaus, or clustered sets of global optimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Optimizer Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pointwise isolation and the corresponding whole-set outer-enclosure criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz continuous, and define \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). A point \(x^*\in X^*\) is nonisolated in \(X^*\) if every \(r>0\) satisfies \[(X^*\setminus\{x^*\})\cap B(x^*,r)\neq\varnothing.\] Such a point has no neighborhood in which it is the unique global optimizer. When the task is to enclose the entire optimizer set at resolution \(\delta>0\), a one-sided outer enclosure is a set \(E_\delta\subseteq X\) satisfying \[X^*\subseteq E_\delta,\qquad \sup_{y\in E_\delta}\operatorname{dist}(y,X^*)\leq\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonisolated optimizer cannot be certified as the unique optimizer in any neighborhood. A whole-set outer-enclosure task instead contains every optimizer and bounds the enclosure's excess distance from the optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
\(x^*\in X^*\) is nonisolated and \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) has no isolating neighborhood; a resolution-\(\delta\) whole-set enclosure satisfies \(X^*\subseteq E_\delta\) and \(\sup_{y\in E_\delta}\operatorname{dist}(y,X^*)\leq\delta\).

children.title: Feasible-Domain Model Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Feasible-domain settings supporting different extension, partition, and constraint-handling families.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Interval Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional Lipschitz global optimization over a closed bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(-\infty<a<b<\infty\) and let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\). A compact interval Lipschitz optimization problem has the form \[\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x),\] where there exists \(L\geq0\) such that \[|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L|x-y|\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in[a,b].\] The objective attains its minimum on \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a real-valued Lipschitz function on a nonempty closed bounded real interval; a global minimizer exists.
assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<a<b<\infty\).
\(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(L\geq0\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L|x-y|\) for all \(x,y\in[a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Lipschitz Global Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Lipschitz minimization over a compact axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\ell_i<u_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and define \[B:=\prod_{i=1}^{n}[\ell_i,u_i]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n.\] Given a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), a box-constrained Lipschitz global optimization problem is \[\min_{x\in B}f(x),\] where \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|\) for all \(x,y\in B\) and some \(L\geq0\). The objective attains its global minimum on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a real-valued Lipschitz function over a compact axis-aligned box in finite-dimensional space.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\ell_i<u_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(L\geq0\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|\) for all \(x,y\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant relative to the specified norm

children.title: Convex Feasible Domains
children.top_down_role: Lipschitz optimization over compact feasible regions possessing convex geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Feasible Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex feasible-domain model used by regularity-based global partition methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\). A nonempty set \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex feasible domain if, for every \(x,y\in D\) and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), \[\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in D.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty feasible domain is convex when it contains every line segment joining two of its points.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in D\) for all \(x,y\in D\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

children.title: Star-Shaped Feasible Domains
children.top_down_role: Lipschitz optimization over feasible regions organized around one or more kernel points.

knowledge_statements.title: Star-Shaped Feasible Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible domains visible by line segments from at least one kernel point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\). A nonempty set \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is star-shaped if there exists \(c\in D\) such that \[[c,x]:=\{(1-t)c+tx:t\in[0,1]\}\subseteq D\] for every \(x\in D\). The kernel \(\ker(D)\) is the set of all such points \(c\). Hence \(D\) is star-shaped if and only if \(\ker(D)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty domain is star-shaped when one feasible center can be joined to every feasible point by a segment lying entirely in the domain; its kernel is the set of all such centers.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is star-shaped if and only if \(\ker(D)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of star centers of the domain

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

children.title: Convex Star-Shaped Specialization
children.top_down_role: Search structures shared by convex domains viewed as a specialized star-shaped regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Star-Shaped Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex domains are star-shaped with every feasible point as a center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) and let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex. For every \(c,x\in D\) and every \(t\in[0,1]\), \[(1-t)c+tx\in D.\] Hence every point of \(D\) is a star center and \(\ker(D)=D\). Consequently, a construction for star-shaped domains that requires a chosen star center may use any feasible point when specialized to a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty convex domain is star-shaped about each of its points, so its star kernel equals the whole domain.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex.

notation.meaning: set of star centers of the domain

children.title: Nonconvex Star-Shaped Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric limitations arising when star-shaped feasibility lacks convexity.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and closed.
There exists \(c\in D\) such that \([c,x]\subset D\) for every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is star-shaped but nonconvex, and \(\partial D=\overline D\setminus\operatorname{int}D\) may contain reentrant or disconnected boundary portions while every radial segment from \(c\) remains feasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Euclidean definitions of star-shapedness, nonconvexity, and boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean feasible domains that retain a star center without being convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) has a nonconvex star-shaped boundary, in this local sense, if there is a point \(c\in D\) satisfying \([c,x]=\{(1-t)c+tx:t\in[0,1]\}\subset D\) for every \(x\in D\), while some \(x,y\in D\) and \(t\in(0,1)\) satisfy \((1-t)x+ty\notin D\). Its boundary is \(\partial D=\overline D\setminus\operatorname{int}D\); star-shapedness constrains radial visibility from \(c\) but does not imply convexity of \(D\) or \(\partial D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain has this boundary type when every point is visible from one feasible star center, yet some segment between two feasible points leaves the domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Star-Shaped Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The star-shaped and nonconvex conditions are standard, but no inspectable citation supports the boundary terminology or the claim about disconnected boundary portions. That claim also needs additional qualifications for the intended class of domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Lipschitz Constraint Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite systems of explicitly evaluable Lipschitz inequalities on a compact Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be explicitly evaluable. An explicit Lipschitz constraint problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_j(x)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where known finite constants \(L_f,L_1,\ldots,L_m\ge 0\) satisfy \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L_f\lVert x-y\rVert\) and \(|g_j(x)-g_j(y)|\le L_j\lVert x-y\rVert\) for all \(x,y\in X\) and every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Feasibility is determined directly from the displayed constraint values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite collection of explicitly evaluable Lipschitz inequalities defines feasibility, and the objective is minimized over the points satisfying all those inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are explicitly evaluable and have stated finite global Lipschitz bounds on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(D=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and the problem is \(\min_{x\in D}f(x)\).

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Hidden Feasibility Constraints
children.top_down_role: Feasibility restrictions revealed only through attempted objective or constraint evaluations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a prescribed search domain.
An evaluation interface reports success with an objective value or failure without exposing all feasibility predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The effective feasible set is \(D=\{x\in X:E(x)\text{ succeeds}\}\), although no explicit complete description of \(D\) is available to the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Black-box feasibility revealed only through whether an attempted objective evaluation succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hidden feasibility constraint is an unexposed predicate whose violation prevents a valid objective observation. Formally, an evaluator \(E\) on \(X\) returns either \(E(x)=f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\) or a failure symbol \(E(x)=\bot\). The effective feasible set is \(D=\{x\in X:E(x)\ne\bot\}\), but the algorithm has neither an explicit defining system for \(D\) nor, absent additional assumptions, information about the distance or direction from a failed point to \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hidden constraint makes feasibility observable only through evaluation success; failure identifies an unusable point but generally gives no explicit constraint value or boundary distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Feasibility Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent for a declared success/failure oracle and fits the leaf, but equating successful evaluation with effective feasibility is model-dependent and currently has no inspectable source.

children.title: Evaluation Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among infeasible, undefined, interrupted, or otherwise unavailable evaluations.

assumptions_latex: Each query returns either a valid value or a recorded failure label.
Failure labels are interpreted only through a declared observation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every failed query is assigned to exactly one declared class, and only classes explicitly identified with infeasibility justify the implication \(E(x)=\bot\Rightarrow x\notin D\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational partition of black-box evaluation outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational classification separating feasibility information from numerical and transient failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the evaluator return either a value in \(\mathbb{R}\) or a label in a disjoint union \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{inf}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{num}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{trans}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{unk}}\). These classes denote certified infeasibility, deterministic numerical or domain failure, transient computational failure, and unclassified failure, respectively. This is an observation taxonomy, not a geometric theorem: only a declared label in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) entails \(x\notin D\); labels in the other classes do not determine feasibility without extra assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failures should be separated into certified infeasibility, deterministic numerical failure, transient failure, and unknown failure; only the first class automatically proves infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation Failure Taxonomy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind, but the four-class taxonomy is a proposed operational convention rather than a standard uniquely determined taxonomy. A source or explicit adopted standard is required.

children.title: Feasibility Inference from Failures
children.top_down_role: Use of failed evaluations as partial evidence about the feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Inference from Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical feasibility information supplied by sound success and certified-failure observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset X\) be unknown, and suppose a sound binary evaluator reports success exactly on \(D\) and certified infeasibility exactly on \(X\setminus D\). For queried points \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), define \(s_i=1\) for success and \(s_i=0\) for certified infeasibility. Then \(s_i=1\Rightarrow x_i\in D\) and \(s_i=0\Rightarrow x_i\notin D\). Without a regularity or shape model for \(D\), the observations impose no membership conclusion at an unqueried point \(x\in X\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound binary evaluator classifies the queried points, but without assumptions on the feasible set it gives no conclusive membership information at unqueried points.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset X\) is unknown.
The evaluator reports success exactly for points in \(D\) and certified infeasibility exactly for points in \(X\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The observations certify \(x_i\in D\) for successes and \(x_i\notin D\) for certified failures, but they do not classify unqueried points without additional assumptions on \(D\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise inference under a sound binary feasibility oracle

children.title: Search Bias from Failed Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Coverage or selection distortions caused by treating unavailable values as feasibility evidence.

assumptions_latex: A search rule updates its sampling distribution using recorded failures.
Some recorded failures are not sound certificates of infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Excluding neighborhoods solely because they contain failures can assign zero future sampling probability to a region containing a global minimizer.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: support loss caused by treating ambiguous failures as infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support loss when ambiguous failures are converted into permanent spatial exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a failed evaluation at \(z\) causes a search rule to choose a neighborhood \(U\ni z\) and impose \(P_n(U)=0\) for every later sampling distribution \(P_n\). If that failure was numerical or transient rather than a sound infeasibility certificate, it is possible that a global minimizer \(x^*\in U\) is feasible. Then \(P_n(B(x^*,r))=0\) for every sufficiently small \(r>0\), so any convergence guarantee requiring persistent positive sampling probability near \(x^*\) no longer applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating an ambiguous failure as permanent infeasibility can remove a neighborhood containing the global minimizer and invalidate global-search convergence conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Search Bias from Failed Evaluations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary correctly captures the terminal role, and the conditional support-loss argument is coherent. A source is still required for the stated convergence-condition interpretation and algorithmic scope.

children.title: Regularity Information Regimes
children.top_down_role: Certified, estimated, regional, and unavailable Lipschitz information arranged from strongest to weakest prior knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Global Lipschitz Constant Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The exact minimal global Lipschitz modulus is known throughout a nonempty metric search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty metric space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be globally Lipschitz. Define its minimal global Lipschitz modulus by \(L_*:=\inf\{L\ge 0: |f(x)-f(y)|\le Ld(x,y)\text{ for all }x,y\in X\}\). The known global Lipschitz constant regime holds when the finite value \(L_*\) is supplied to the algorithm. Every observation \((x_i,f(x_i))\) then yields \(f(x_i)-L_*d(x,x_i)\le f(x)\le f(x_i)+L_*d(x,x_i)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact minimal global Lipschitz modulus is supplied, so each observation gives globally valid upper and lower cones without a regularity-estimation margin.

\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is globally Lipschitz.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Constant Upper-Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proved upper bound is known although the exact minimal global modulus need not be known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a nonempty metric space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be globally Lipschitz, with minimal global modulus \(L_*:=\inf\{L\ge 0: |f(x)-f(y)|\le Ld(x,y)\text{ for all }x,y\in X\}\). The certified constant upper-bound regime holds when a proved finite value \(\widehat L\ge L_*\) is supplied although \(L_*\) itself need not be known. Then \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le\widehat Ld(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\), and \(f(x_i)-\widehat Ld(x,x_i)\) is a valid global lower bound. For fixed \(x\) and \(x_i\), this lower bound is nonincreasing as \(\widehat L\) increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified finite overestimate of the minimal global Lipschitz modulus preserves valid global bounds, while larger overestimates make the lower cones no tighter.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Region Regularity Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity certificates governing comparisons between distinct local search regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty regions \(R_i,R_j\subset X\), cross-region regularity information for \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a certified finite constant \(M_{ij}\) satisfying \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le M_{ij}d(x,y)\) for every \(x\in R_i\) and \(y\in R_j\). If \(R_i\cap R_j\ne\varnothing\), then for every \(z\in R_i\cap R_j\), \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L_i d(x,z)+L_j d(z,y)\) holds for all \(x\in R_i\) and \(y\in R_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-region information is a certified bound for pairs drawn from different regions. Separate within-region bounds do not provide it for disjoint regions, while overlapping regions can be linked through any shared point.

knowledge_statements.title: Anisotropic Bound Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional constants are aggregated through a weighted \(\ell_1\) metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative directional constants \(L_1,\ldots,L_n\), define the anisotropic pseudometric \[d_L(x,y)=\sum_{j=1}^nL_j|x_j-y_j|.\] If \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le d_L(x,y)\) on a box \(R\), then a sample \(s\in R\) induces the minorant \(q_s(x)=f(s)-d_L(x,s)\). Its regional value is \[\min_{x\in R}q_s(x)=f(s)-\sum_{j=1}^nL_j\max\{s_j-\ell_j,u_j-s_j\}.\] Thus each coordinate penalty is aggregated additively without replacing the constants by a single isotropic maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted Manhattan metric aggregates unequal directional constants into an explicit regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R=\prod_j[\ell_j,u_j]\) and \(s\in R\).
\(|f(x)-f(y)|\le d_L(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_s\le f\) on \(R\), with the displayed exact minimum of \(q_s\).

children.title: Regional Directionality Validity
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting transfer of directional information across a search region.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Directionality Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity is required on every coordinate-parallel segment contained in the current box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be an axis-aligned box, let \(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(L_1,\ldots,L_n\ge 0\). The directional data are valid on \(R\) precisely when, for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and every \(x,y\in R\) satisfying \(x_k=y_k\) for all \(k\ne j\), \[|f(x)-f(y)|\le L_j|x_j-y_j|.\] Under this condition, coordinate-replacement paths remain in \(R\), and every \(x,y\in R\) satisfy \[|f(x)-f(y)|\le\sum_{j=1}^n L_j|x_j-y_j|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional constants are regionally valid when they control every corresponding coordinate-parallel segment in the box; this condition yields the weighted coordinatewise Lipschitz inequality throughout the box.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is an axis-aligned box.
\(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(L_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinatewise condition implies \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le\sum_{j=1}^nL_j|x_j-y_j|\) for all \(x,y\in R\).

notation.meaning: region on which validity is asserted

children.title: Geometric Lipschitz Minorants

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Centered Lower Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Lipschitz observation defines a norm cone lying below the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz with respect to a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \(x_i\in D\) be sampled. The sample-centered lower cone is \[q_i(x)=f(x_i)-L\|x-x_i\|,\qquad x\in D.\] The Lipschitz inequality gives \(q_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), while \(q_i(x_i)=f(x_i)\). Hence \(q_i\) is a globally valid minorant anchored exactly at the observed sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each sampled value supports a downward Lipschitz cone that underestimates the objective everywhere and touches it at the sample.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(D\) in the selected norm.
\(x_i\in D\) and \(L\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_i(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in D\), and \(q_i(x_i)=f(x_i)\).

notation.meaning: lower cone centered at sample i

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-of-Cones Lower Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sample cones combine by pointwise maximization into a valid cone-derived minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz with respect to a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset D\) with \(m\ge1\). Define \[Q_S(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\bigl\{f(x_i)-L\|x-x_i\|\bigr\},\qquad x\in D.\] Then \(Q_S(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), and \(Q_S\) pointwise dominates each constituent cone. If \(R\subseteq D\) is nonempty and compact, then \[B(S,R)=\min_{x\in R}Q_S(x)\] is a valid scalar lower bound on \(f\) over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise maximum of finitely many sampled lower cones remains a valid minorant, dominates each individual cone, and yields a regional lower bound when minimized over a compact region.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset D\) with \(m\ge1\).
\(R\subseteq D\) is nonempty and compact for attainment of the minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_S\le f\) on \(D\), and \(B(S,R)\le\min_{x\in R}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Lower-Bound Characteristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two endpoint cones give an exact scalar characteristic for a one-dimensional interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, with \(L>0\). The endpoint-cone envelope is \[Q(x)=\max\{f(a)-L(x-a),\ f(b)-L(b-x)\}.\] Endpoint consistency \(|f(a)-f(b)|\le L(b-a)\) places the intersection of the two affine pieces in \([a,b]\), and therefore \[\min_{x\in[a,b]}Q(x)=\frac{f(a)+f(b)-L(b-a)}{2}.\] This characteristic is a certified lower bound on \(\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, minimizing the envelope of the two endpoint cones gives the standard explicit Lipschitz lower characteristic.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(f(a)+f(b)-L(b-a)\bigr)/2\le\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Region Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opposite-corner samples produce a certified bound through their two-center covering radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a box whose opposite vertices are \(a\) and \(b\), and suppose \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(R\). Define the two-corner covering radius \[\rho_R=\max_{x\in R}\min\{\|x-a\|,\|x-b\|\}.\] The diagonal-endpoint envelope satisfies \[f(x)\ge\max\{f(a)-L\|x-a\|,f(b)-L\|x-b\|\}\ge\min\{f(a),f(b)\}-L\rho_R.\] Hence the final expression is a certified lower bound for the whole box, not merely for its main diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite-corner observations bound a box using the maximum distance from any point to its nearer sampled corner.
assumptions_latex: \(R=[a,b]\) is a compact axis-aligned box.
\(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(R\).

children.title: Bound Validity-Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Navigation among tight, conservative, invalid, and spatially nonuniform regularity bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Tight Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightness means equality between the envelope minimum and the true regional minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, let \(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, let \(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset R\) with \(m\ge1\), and define \[Q_S(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{f(x_i)-L\|x-x_i\|\}.\] The bound is tight on \(R\) precisely when \[\min_{x\in R}Q_S(x)=\min_{x\in R}f(x).\] Equivalently, writing \(f_R^*=\min_{x\in R}f(x)\), tightness holds precisely when \[Q_S(x)\ge f_R^*\qquad\text{for every }x\in R.\] In the tight regime, every \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)\) satisfies \(Q_S(x^*)=f(x^*)\), so at least one sampled cone is saturated at \(x^*\). Cone contact at a minimizer alone is not sufficient for tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope bound is tight exactly when its value never falls below the true regional minimum. Tightness forces sampled-cone contact at every regional minimizer, but contact at one minimizer alone does not guarantee tightness.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact.
\(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset R\) with \(m\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tightness is equivalent to \(Q_S(x)\ge f_R^*\) for every \(x\in R\), and it implies cone contact at every regional minimizer.

notation.meaning: true minimum value of f over R

children.title: Certified Conservative Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Conservative Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An upper bound on the true Lipschitz modulus certifies every resulting cone minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_*\), and let \(\widehat L\ge L_*\) be certified. For every sample \(x_i\in D\), \[f(x_i)-\widehat L\|x-x_i\|\le f(x_i)-L_*\|x-x_i\|\le f(x),\qquad x\in D.\] Consequently, for any finite sample set \(S\) and region \(R\subseteq D\), \[\min_{x\in R}\max_{x_i\in S}\{f(x_i)-\widehat L\|x-x_i\|\}\le\min_{x\in R}f(x).\] The verifiable inequality \(\widehat L\ge L_*\) is therefore a validity certificate, although it need not ensure a sharp bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any certified overestimate of the Lipschitz modulus preserves validity of all sample-cone regional lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has true Lipschitz modulus no greater than \(L_*\).
\(\widehat L\ge L_*\).
\(S\subset D\) is finite and \(R\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The envelope formed with \(\widehat L\) is a certified minorant of \(f\).

notation.meaning: true or certified upper Lipschitz modulus
conservative constant used by the bound

children.title: Severe Constant Overestimation

knowledge_statements.title: Severe Constant Overestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded constant inflation makes finite-sample cone-envelope bounds vacuous when the region contains a point separated from all samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset R\) with \(m\ge1\), and suppose that some \(x_0\in R\) satisfies \[\delta=\min_{1\le i\le m}\|x_0-x_i\|>0.\] Assume that every sampled value \(f(x_i)\) is finite. For \(\widehat L>0\), define \[Q_{\widehat L}(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{f(x_i)-\widehat L\|x-x_i\|\},\qquad B_{\widehat L}=\inf_{x\in R}Q_{\widehat L}(x).\] Then \[B_{\widehat L}\le Q_{\widehat L}(x_0)\le\max_{1\le i\le m}f(x_i)-\widehat L\delta,\] and consequently \[B_{\widehat L}\to-\infty\qquad\text{as }\widehat L\to\infty.\] Thus arbitrary constant overestimation can preserve minorant validity while destroying finite-sample informativeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the region contains a point at positive distance from every sample, increasing the cone constant without bound drives the regional cone-envelope lower bound to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset R\) is finite and nonempty.
Some \(x_0\in R\) has positive distance \(\delta\) from \(S\).
Each sampled value \(f(x_i)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{\widehat L}\to-\infty\) as \(\widehat L\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: distance of a regional point from the finite sample set
cone envelope formed with the inflated constant
infimum of the cone envelope over the region

children.title: Overestimation Efficiency Loss

knowledge_statements.title: Overestimation Efficiency Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant inflation weakens regional bounds monotonically and linearly for a single underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sample \(s\in R\), let \(r_R(s)=\max_{x\in R}\|x-s\|\) and define the single-cone bound \(b_L(R)=f(s)-Lr_R(s)\). If \(\widehat L\ge L\), then \[b_{\widehat L}(R)=b_L(R)-(\widehat L-L)r_R(s)\le b_L(R).\] More generally, every finite maximum-of-cones regional bound is nonincreasing in the constant used to form its cones. Hence overestimation enlarges the lower-bound gap; for the single-cone construction, the exact loss equals \((\widehat L-L)r_R(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing a valid Lipschitz constant weakens cone bounds; with one sample, the loss equals constant inflation times regional radius.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is compact and \(s\in R\).
\(0\le L\le\widehat L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_L(R)-b_{\widehat L}(R)=(\widehat L-L)r_R(s)\), and cone-envelope bounds are nonincreasing in the chosen constant.

notation.meaning: single-cone regional bound using constant L

knowledge_statements.title: Conservatism Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition law for Lipschitz cone bounds as the supplied constant crosses the true constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) have least Lipschitz constant \(L_*\) on a metric space \((X,d)\), and let sampled sites be \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). For \(K\ge0\), define \(\ell_K(x)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\{f(x_i)-K d(x,x_i)\}\). If \(K\ge L_*\), then \(\ell_K(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\); increasing \(K\) preserves validity and decreases the bound pointwise. At \(K=L_*\) the bound is least conservative within this family. For \(K<L_*\), validity is not guaranteed: some admissible function and point can satisfy \(\ell_K(x)>f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossing the true Lipschitz constant separates potentially invalid bounds from valid ones; above it, larger constants yield progressively weaker lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is globally Lipschitz on \(X\).
The sampled function values are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\ge L_*\Rightarrow \ell_K\le f\), while \(K<L_*\) does not guarantee this inequality.

notation.meaning: least global Lipschitz constant of the objective
sample-based Lipschitz lower envelope using constant K

knowledge_statements.title: Underestimated Constant Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of a cone lower bound formed with an underestimated Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), let \(f(x)=-Lx\) with \(L>0\), and suppose only \(x_0=0\) is sampled. If the model uses \(0\le K<L\), its cone bound is \(\ell_K(x)=f(0)-K|x|=-Kx\). For every \(x\in(0,1]\), \(\ell_K(x)-f(x)=(L-K)x>0\). Thus \(\ell_K\) is not a lower bound, and its nominal lower value \(-K\) exceeds the true minimum \(-L\). Consequently, a stopping test based on this invalid bound can falsely certify an accuracy gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear function shows that underestimating the Lipschitz constant can place the supposed lower bound above the objective and invalidate certificates.
assumptions_latex: Only the exact value at \(x_0=0\) is initially available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_K(x)>f(x)\) for all \(x\in(0,1]\).

notation.meaning: underestimated constant used by the bound

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Nonuniform Local Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Efficiency boundary for a globally valid cone model when regional Lipschitz constants vary greatly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\bigcup_{j=1}^m R_j\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be globally Lipschitz with a valid constant \(K\), and suppose the restriction of \(f\) to each \(R_j\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L_j\le K\). For sampled \(y\in R_j\) and any \(x\in R_j\), compare the globally valid cone \(c_K(x)=f(y)-K d(x,y)\) with the regional cone \(c_j(x)=f(y)-L_j d(x,y)\). Then \[c_j(x)-c_K(x)=(K-L_j)d(x,y).\] Thus the globally valid cone can lie arbitrarily far below the corresponding regional cone, relative to distance, as \(K/L_j\) grows. This loss of local tightness can weaken pruning, although it does not invalidate the global cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a valid global constant greatly exceeds a regional Lipschitz constant, its cone is lower than the corresponding regional cone by the constant difference times distance. The global bound stays valid but may prune poorly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is globally \(K\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
For each \(j\), the restriction \(f|_{R_j}\) is \(L_j\)-Lipschitz and \(0\le L_j\le K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(x,y\in R_j\), \(c_j(x)-c_K(x)=(K-L_j)d(x,y)\), so local tightness may deteriorate without loss of global validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Grid Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Passive minimization of a univariate Lipschitz function on an equally spaced grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\), an integer \(n\ge1\), and grid spacing \(h=(b-a)/n\), evaluate \(f\) at \(x_i=a+ih\) for \(i=0,\ldots,n\). Return \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le i\le n}f(x_i)\). If \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\), some grid point lies within \(h/2\) of \(x^*\); hence \(0\le f(\hat x)-f(x^*)\le Lh/2\). Thus \(n\ge L(b-a)/(2\varepsilon)\) suffices for absolute error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate an equally spaced grid and return its best point; Lipschitz continuity converts grid spacing into a deterministic error guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the compact interval \([a,b]\).
Function evaluations are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\hat x)-\min_{[a,b]}f\le L(b-a)/(2n)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Passive Lipschitz Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case guarantee for sample sites fixed independently of observed objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_n=\{x_1,ldots,x_n\}\subset[a,b]\) be selected independently of the observed values of an \(L\)-Lipschitz function \(f\), and return \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in S_n}f(x_i)\). Define the covering radius \(r(S_n)=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}\min_{x_i\in S_n}|x-x_i|\). For every such \(f\), \(0\le f(\hat x)-\min_{[a,b]}f\le Lr(S_n)\). Conversely, for any fixed \(S_n\), the function \(f_S(x)=-L\min_{x_i\in S_n}|x-x_i|\) makes the error equal to \(Lr(S_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed sample sites, worst-case Lipschitz optimization error equals the Lipschitz constant times their covering radius.
assumptions_latex: \(S_n\) is chosen without using sampled function values.
The output is the best sampled point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le L}\bigl(f(\hat x)-\min f\bigr)=Lr(S_n)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Envelope Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-envelope lower model used by the univariate Piyavskii–Shubert method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and let exact values \(f(x_i)\) be known at distinct sites \(x_1,ldots,x_n\). Define
\[p_n(x)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\bigl(f(x_i)-L|x-x_i|\bigr).\]
Every sampled cone is a lower bound, so \(p_n(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\), while \(p_n(x_i)=f(x_i)\). Therefore \(B_n=\min_{x\in[a,b]}p_n(x)\) is a certified lower bound on \(f^*=\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\). Adding a sample replaces \(p_n\) by a pointwise no-smaller envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of downward Lipschitz cones from sampled values interpolates the samples and supplies a monotone certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \([a,b]\).
The constant \(L\) is valid and sampled values are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_n\le f\) and \(B_n=\min p_n\le f^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Interval-Partition Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval characteristics and adaptive refinement underlying Piyavskii–Shubert search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the sampled sites as \(a=x_1<\cdots<x_n=b\), write \(f_i=f(x_i)\), and assume \(|f_{i+1}-f_i|\le L(x_{i+1}-x_i)\). On each interval \([x_i,x_{i+1}]\), the two adjacent cones meet at \[z_i=\frac{x_i+x_{i+1}}{2}+\frac{f_i-f_{i+1}}{2L},\qquad R_i=\frac{f_i+f_{i+1}}{2}-\frac{L(x_{i+1}-x_i)}{2}.\] Here \(R_i\) is the interval lower characteristic. The adaptive partition selects an index in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i<n}R_i\), evaluates \(f(z_i)\), and replaces \([x_i,x_{i+1}]\) by \([x_i,z_i]\) and \([z_i,x_{i+1}]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each sampled interval has a computable cone-intersection lower characteristic; the method splits an interval having the smallest characteristic.
assumptions_latex: \(L>0\) is a valid Lipschitz constant.
Both endpoints of \([a,b]\) have been evaluated, and the sampled sites are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition update inserts \(z_i\) for some \(i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le k<n}R_k\).

notation.meaning: intersection point of the adjacent endpoint cones on interval i

knowledge_statements.title: Piyavskii–Shubert Accuracy Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori objective-value certificate from the incumbent and lower-envelope values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and suppose \(a=x_1<\cdots<x_n=b\) have been evaluated exactly. Let \(p_n\) be the corresponding Lipschitz lower envelope, define \(U_n=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\), \(B_n=\min_{x\in[a,b]}p_n(x)=\min_{1\le i<n}R_i\), and let \(f^*=\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\). Then \(B_n\le f^*\le U_n\). Hence \(G_n=U_n-B_n\) satisfies \[0\le f(\hat x_n)-f^*\le G_n\] for every sampled incumbent \(\hat x_n\) with \(f(\hat x_n)=U_n\). Therefore \(G_n\le\varepsilon\) certifies that \(\hat x_n\) is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal in objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With both endpoints sampled, the best observed value minus the minimum lower-envelope characteristic bounds the incumbent's objective error and gives a rigorous stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \([a,b]\), with the valid constant \(L\) used by the envelope.
The sampled set includes \(a\) and \(b\), and all evaluations are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_n\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow 0\le f(\hat x_n)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified minimum of the lower envelope

knowledge_statements.title: Piyavskii–Shubert Optimizer Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Location of a lower-envelope minimizer within the current sampled partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(a=x_1<\cdots<x_n=b\), and let \(L>0\) be a valid Lipschitz constant. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}\), define \(z_i\) and \(R_i\) by the adjacent-cone intersection formulas. Then \(z_i\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]\), and \[\min_{x\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]}p_n(x)=p_n(z_i)=R_i.\] Consequently, \[\min_{x\in[a,b]}p_n(x)=\min_{1\le i<n}R_i,\] and for every \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i<n}R_i\), the point \(z_{i^*}\) is a global minimizer of \(p_n\). Such a point may be used as the next Piyavskii–Shubert trial point; ties may be resolved arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower envelope reaches its minimum at an adjacent-cone intersection, so any interval with the smallest characteristic supplies a valid next trial point.
assumptions_latex: The exact sampled sites include both endpoints and satisfy \(a=x_1<\cdots<x_n=b\).
\(L>0\) is a valid Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i<n}R_i\), then \(z_{i^*}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}p_n(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Evtushenko Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional univariate Lipschitz branch-and-bound formulation; historical variant requires source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\), a valid constant \(L>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), initialize a partition with evaluated endpoints. For every current interval \([u,v]\), compute the Lipschitz lower bound \(R(u,v)=(f(u)+f(v)-L(v-u))/2\) and its cone-intersection point \(z(u,v)=(u+v)/2+(f(u)-f(v))/(2L)\). Repeatedly select an interval of smallest \(R\), evaluate \(f\) at its \(z\), and split it there. Return the best sampled point when the incumbent value minus the smallest current lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This provisional formulation repeatedly splits the interval with the smallest Lipschitz lower bound and stops when its certified gap is small.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is Lipschitz on \([a,b]\) with known valid constant \(L\).
Evaluations are exact.

children.title: Timonov Search Method

knowledge_statements.title: Timonov Search Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional lower-envelope search template; Timonov-specific selection rule requires authoritative sourcing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be evaluated initially at a finite set \(S_0\) containing \(a\) and \(b\), and let \(L>0\) be valid. At iteration \(n\), form \(p_n(x)=\max_{t\in S_n}\{f(t)-L|x-t|\}\), select \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}p_n(x)\), evaluate \(f(x_{n+1})\), and set \(S_{n+1}=S_n\cup\{x_{n+1}\}\). With \(U_n=min_{t\in S_n}f(t)\) and \(B_n=min_xp_n(x)\), stop when \(U_n-B_n\le\varepsilon\) and return a sampled minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This provisional template samples where the current Lipschitz lower envelope is smallest and stops using the envelope-incumbent gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has known valid Lipschitz constant \(L>0\).
All evaluations are exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian Reading of Timonov Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-theoretic reading of a deterministic Lipschitz lower-envelope rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations be \(D_n=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\), where \(y_i=f(x_i)\), and let \(L>0\). Define the feasible lower envelope \(\ell_n(x)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\{y_i-L|x-x_i|\}\). A Bayesian reading of a Timonov-type selection rule is valid at stage \(n\) only when a specified prior and loss produce an acquisition function \(A_n\) satisfying \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in[a,b]}A_n(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}\ell_n(x)\). The equality concerns decisions; it does not by itself identify \(\ell_n\) as a posterior mean or credible bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bayesian interpretation is decision-equivalence: a specified Bayesian acquisition rule must select exactly the minimizers of the deterministic Lipschitz lower envelope.
assumptions_latex: \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) is observed without noise.
\(|f(x)-f(z)|\le L|x-z|\) for all \(x,z\in[a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}A_n=\operatorname*{argmin}\ell_n\) is the required decision correspondence.

notation.meaning: Bayesian acquisition function under a specified prior and loss

Do not infer a probabilistic posterior from the deterministic envelope alone.

children.title: Timonov–Bayesian Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Timonov–Bayesian Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagewise equivalence criterion for deterministic and Bayesian sampling policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_n:I_n\to\mathbb R\) be the Timonov interval characteristic on the current partition \(I_n\), with smaller values preferred, and let \(B_n:I_n\to\mathbb R\) be the Bayesian interval score, with larger values preferred. The two policies correspond stagewise precisely when their preference preorders agree: for every \(J,K\in I_n\), \(T_n(J)\le T_n(K)\) if and only if \(B_n(J)\ge B_n(K)\), and both policies use the same measurable tie-breaking and within-interval sampling rule. Under these conditions they generate identical evaluation sequences from the same initial data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policies correspond only when their interval rankings, tie-breaking, and within-interval sample locations agree at every stage.
assumptions_latex: \(I_n\) is the same finite interval partition for both policies.
Both scores are determined by the same observation history.

Method-specific source needed before replacing this abstract equivalence criterion.

children.title: Bayesian Interpretation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian Interpretation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of interpreting Lipschitz optimism as Bayesian inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic Lipschitz rule based only on \(D_n\) and \(L\) does not determine a unique probability law on functions. Consequently, equality between its next evaluation and a Bayesian acquisition maximizer establishes neither equality of posterior distributions nor calibrated posterior probabilities. The interpretation fails as a full Bayesian equivalence whenever no prior, observation model, loss, and tie-breaking convention are specified, or whenever the resulting Bayesian policy assigns a different ordering to two admissible intervals. Decision coincidence at finitely many stages is therefore weaker than probabilistic-model equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching sample choices does not establish posterior equivalence; a prior, likelihood, loss, and matching rankings are additionally required.
assumptions_latex: \(D_n\) contains finitely many exact observations.
The deterministic rule uses only Lipschitz feasibility information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{decision coincidence}\not\Rightarrow\text{posterior-law equivalence}\).
review_flags: Standard decision-theoretic distinction, but a source addressing the Timonov interpretation specifically is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary correctly separates finite decision coincidence from posterior-law equivalence, but the record has no source connecting this distinction to the Timonov interpretation in the immutable path.

knowledge_statements.title: Schoen Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional lower-bound partition formulation; historical normalization requires confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an interval \([a,b]\), exact evaluations of an \(L\)-Lipschitz function, and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Maintain a partition with sampled endpoints. For each adjacent pair \(u<v\), compute \(r(u,v)=(f(u)+f(v)-L(v-u))/2\) and \(z(u,v)=(u+v)/2+(f(u)-f(v))/(2L)\). Select an interval of minimum \(r\), evaluate \(f\) at its clipped point \(z\), and split that interval. With incumbent \(U=\min_i f(x_i)\), stop when \(U-\min r\le\varepsilon\), returning an incumbent minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Galperin Univariate Method

knowledge_statements.title: Hansen–Jaumard–Lu Two-Phase Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract two-phase enclosure-and-refinement scheme pending method-specific verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(L\)-Lipschitz function on \([a,b]\), maintain sampled points, the incumbent \(U\), and interval lower bounds \(R(J)\). Phase I repeatedly discards every interval \(J\) satisfying \(R(J)>U-\varepsilon\) and subdivides a retained interval of minimum \(R(J)\), until the surviving union \(S\) consists only of intervals that may contain an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer. Phase II refines every component of \(S\) until its diameter is at most \(\delta\). Output \(S\) and the best sampled point.

knowledge_statements.title: Basso Revision of Piyavskii Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-minimizer-preserving revision formulated through cone-envelope screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given exact samples \((x_i,f(x_i))\) and a valid Lipschitz constant \(L\), form \(\ell_n(x)=\max_i\{f(x_i)-L|x-x_i|\}\) and \(U_n=\min_i f(x_i)\). Retain every connected component of \(C_n(\varepsilon)=\{x\in[a,b]:\ell_n(x)\le U_n+\varepsilon\}\); sample and subdivide all retained components according to a fair rule, rather than following only one best component. Stop for location tolerance \(\delta\) when every retained component has diameter at most \(\delta\), and output their union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserve and refine every interval that the Lipschitz envelope cannot exclude, allowing all global minimizers to remain enclosed.
assumptions_latex: \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.

The all-components fairness rule is mathematically sufficient but historically unverified here.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Optimizer Enclosure Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Evaluation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case deterministic evaluation bound for one-dimensional Lipschitz minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz and let \(\varepsilon>0\). Evaluate \(f\) on a uniform grid whose spacing is at most \(2\varepsilon/L\), and return the best grid point \(\widehat x\). Every global minimizer is within half a grid spacing of some evaluated point, so \(f(\widehat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\). Thus exact value-oracle minimization to objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires no more than \(N=\lceil L(b-a)/(2\varepsilon)\rceil+1\) evaluations by this construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform grid achieves objective error epsilon using at most ceiling of Lipschitz constant times interval length over twice epsilon, plus one evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a sequential univariate scheme begins with exactly two evaluations, at \(a\) and \(b\), and each completed refinement iteration evaluates exactly one previously unevaluated point. If the scheme reaches objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) after \(M(\varepsilon)\) total evaluations, then its actual refinement count is \(M(\varepsilon)-2\). Consequently, if \(M(\varepsilon)\le N(\varepsilon)\), then \(K(\varepsilon)\le\max\{0,N(\varepsilon)-2\}\). For a sequential realization of the uniform-grid construction with \(N(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil L(b-a)/(2\varepsilon)\right\rceil+1\), this gives \(K(\varepsilon)\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil L(b-a)/(2\varepsilon)\right\rceil-1\right\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-to-Iteration Relationships
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting identity for sequential and batched univariate partition searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_0\) be the number of initialization evaluations and let \(b_j\geq 0\) be the number of previously unevaluated points sampled during iteration \(j\). After \(k\) completed iterations, the total number of distinct objective evaluations is \[N_k=N_0+\sum_{j=1}^{k}b_j.\] Consequently, a sequential method satisfying \(b_j=1\) has \(N_k=N_0+k\). If instead \(1\leq b_j\leq B\), then \(N_0+k\leq N_k\leq N_0+Bk\). Thus an evaluation bound converts to an iteration bound only after the batch-size convention and initialization cost are specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation and iteration counts differ by initialization and batch size; for one new sample per iteration, their difference is constant.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Dependent Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case deterministic evaluation complexity for one-dimensional Lipschitz minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, let \(D=b-a\), and measure accuracy by simple regret \(f(\widehat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\). In the deterministic value-oracle model, uniform sampling with mesh width at most \(2\varepsilon/L\) returns an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal point using at most \(\lceil LD/(2\varepsilon)\rceil+1\) evaluations. Conversely, adversarial Lipschitz functions hidden between sampled points imply a worst-case requirement of order \(LD/\varepsilon\). Hence the evaluation complexity is \(\Theta(LD/\varepsilon)\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), while it is constant when \(\varepsilon\geq LD\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case deterministic univariate Lipschitz optimization requires order LD/ε evaluations in the high-accuracy regime.
assumptions_latex: \(L>0\), \(D>0\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
Only exact point values of \(f\) are returned.
Performance is worst-case over all \(L\)-Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(\varepsilon)=\Theta(LD/\varepsilon)\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Efficiency Under Constant Overestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of replacing the true Lipschitz constant by a fixed conservative estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) have Lipschitz constant \(L>0\), and let a valid lower-envelope partition method use \(M=cL\) with fixed \(c\geq1\). Every cone \(f(x_i)-M|x-x_i|\) remains a global lower bound for \(f\), so certificate-based convergence is preserved. Any covering argument whose evaluation bound is linear in the supplied constant changes from \(O(LD/\varepsilon)\) to \(O(MD/\varepsilon)=O(cLD/\varepsilon)\). Thus fixed overestimation preserves the accuracy order but may enlarge its leading constant and produce looser lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed conservative Lipschitz estimate preserves correctness and the 1/ε order, but can worsen constants proportionally to its overestimation factor.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on an interval of length \(D\).
\(M=cL\) with fixed \(c\geq1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Method Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-based comparison of valid univariate Lipschitz search methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two methods have evaluated the same set \(S_k\subset[a,b]\), share incumbent \(U_k=\min_{x_i\in S_k}f(x_i)\), and construct valid lower models \(q_k^{(r)}\leq f\), with bounds \(B_k^{(r)}=\min_x q_k^{(r)}(x)\), for \(r\in\{1,2\}\). If \(q_k^{(1)}(x)\geq q_k^{(2)}(x)\) for every \(x\), then \(B_k^{(1)}\geq B_k^{(2)}\) and \(U_k-B_k^{(1)}\leq U_k-B_k^{(2)}\). Therefore the first method has a certificate no weaker at that common sample state, although this pointwise comparison alone does not order future evaluation counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At identical samples, a tighter valid lower model yields a tighter optimality certificate, but need not imply fewer future evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Both lower models are valid on \([a,b]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Piyavskii Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive coordinate reduction for Lipschitz optimization on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=I_1\times\cdots\times I_d\), define recursively \(V_d(x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1})=\min_{x_d\in I_d}f(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\) and eliminate the remaining coordinates analogously. A nested Piyavskii method approximates each one-dimensional minimization by a Lipschitz lower-envelope search. At every outer trial, the required inner problem is solved to a prescribed tolerance; the resulting value and accumulated inner error define valid outer lower and upper bounds. The algorithm stops when the outer incumbent minus the propagated global lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\), and returns the assembled coordinate vector attaining the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method recursively solves coordinatewise Lipschitz subproblems and propagates inner errors into a certified outer stopping test.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous and coordinatewise Lipschitz on the compact box \(X\).
Every inner solver returns certified lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with certificate gap at most \(\varepsilon\) returns an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Extended Univariate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of univariate Lipschitz search through box diagonals and refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a partition of a compact box \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) into subboxes \(R=[u,v]\). On each \(R\), parameterize its principal diagonal by \(x_R(t)=u+t(v-u)\), \(t\in[0,1]\); the restriction \(g_R(t)=f(x_R(t))\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L\lVert v-u\rVert\). Apply a univariate Lipschitz rule to choose diagonal trials, attach a valid lower bound for all of \(R\), select a box having smallest bound, and subdivide it. Stop when the incumbent minus the minimum box bound is at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise continue so that selected box diameters tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method applies univariate Lipschitz searches along box diagonals while refining boxes and retaining valid whole-box lower bounds.

Each diagonal calculation yields a valid lower bound for its entire box.
The refinement rule is exhaustive for boxes that can contain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certificate gap at most \(\varepsilon\) yields an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer; exhaustive refinement gives convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Piyavskii Multivariate Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multivariate Lipschitz lower-envelope method on a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sampled points \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\in X\), form the Lipschitz lower envelope \[H_k(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}\{f(x_i)-L\lVert x-x_i\rVert\}.\] Compute \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}H_k(x)\), evaluate \(f(x_{k+1})\), and set \(U_{k+1}=\min_{i\leq k+1}f(x_i)\). With \(B_k=\min_{x\in X}H_k(x)\), stop when \(U_k-B_k\leq\varepsilon\) and return an incumbent minimizer. If the envelope subproblem is solved globally and \(L\) is valid, \(B_k\leq f^*\), so the stopping test certifies global accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly minimizes the maximum of sampled Lipschitz cones and stops when its lower bound meets the incumbent within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
Each lower-envelope minimization is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\leq f^*\leq U_k\), and \(U_k-B_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Mladineo Method

knowledge_statements.title: Piyavskii–Mladineo Structural Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Method-Specific Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and tractability boundaries for single-envelope multivariate Lipschitz methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the cone envelope \(H_k(x)=\max_i\{f(x_i)-M\lVert x-x_i\rVert\}\), certified exactness requires \(M\) to be a valid Lipschitz upper bound and requires global minimization, or certified bounding, of \(H_k\) over the feasible set. If \(M<L\), a cone can exceed \(f\), so \(\min_X H_k\) need not be a lower bound and the gap test can terminate incorrectly. If envelope minimization is only local, the reported minimum may likewise exceed the true envelope minimum. Noncompact domains additionally require coercivity or a bounded localization containing a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating the Lipschitz constant, locally minimizing the envelope, or using an unlocalized noncompact domain destroys the standard certificate.
assumptions_latex: The method derives its certificate from a sampled Lipschitz-cone envelope.
The objective's actual Lipschitz modulus is \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified use requires \(M\geq L\), certified global envelope minimization, and compactness or valid localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Mayne–Polak Method

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a compact box \(X\) into boxes \(R\). Select a box with minimal \(b(R)\), bisect it along a longest edge, evaluate centers not previously sampled, and update the incumbent \(U\). With \(B=\min_R b(R)\), stop when \(U-B\leq\varepsilon\). If longest-edge refinement is continued, selected box radii vanish and the bound gap supplies a global accuracy certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Wood Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract single-underestimator form; the Wood-specific construction requires source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact feasible set \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), a continuous objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and a partition \(\mathcal P_k\) of active regions, associate with every \(R\in\mathcal P_k\) one computable function \(u_R:R\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(u_R(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in R\). Stop when the incumbent minus \(\min_R L_R\) is at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Galperin Multivariate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract multivariate Lipschitz tree-search form; Galperin-specific selection and partition rules need confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|\). Maintain a rooted tree whose leaves are regions \(R\) covering \(D\). For each leaf choose a sampled point \(c_R\in R\), radius \(r_R=\sup_{x\in R}\|x-c_R\|\), and bound \(B_R=f(c_R)-Lr_R\). Stop when the incumbent minus \(\min_R B_R\) is at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic pointer-based regional tree search; the historically intended pointer rule needs a primary locator.

Return the incumbent when \(U_k-B_{p_k}\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Branching Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite rooted-tree representation of successive regional partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regional branching structure on a nonempty compact set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a rooted, locally finite tree \(T\) with a nonempty compact region \(R_v\subseteq D\) assigned to each node \(v\), such that \(R_{\mathrm{root}}=D\). Every internal node has a finite nonempty set of children satisfying \[R_v=\bigcup_{w\text{ child of }v}R_w,\qquad \operatorname{int}(R_w)\cap\operatorname{int}(R_{w'})=\varnothing\quad(w\ne w').\] An active frontier is obtained from the root by finitely many operations that replace one frontier node by all of its children. The structure is exhaustive if every infinite branch \((v_k)_{k\ge 0}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{v_k})\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional branching structure is a finite-arity region tree whose children cover their parent and have disjoint interiors. Its active frontiers are generated by finite leaf replacements, and it is exhaustive when regions shrink to zero diameter along every infinite branch.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact.
Every assigned region is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every active frontier covers \(D\), and distinct frontier regions have disjoint interiors.

children.title: Lipschitz Bounding Mechanisms

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Bounding Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-sample lower bounds for a Lipschitz objective on a compact region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz under a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), let \(R\subseteq D\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(S_R\subseteq R\) be finite and nonempty. Then \[\ell_R(x)=\max_{s\in S_R}\{f(s)-L\|x-s\|\}\le f(x)\qquad(x\in R),\] and hence \[B_R=\inf_{x\in R}\ell_R(x)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x).\] For a single sample \(c_R\in R\), the bound \[f(c_R)-L\sup_{x\in R}\|x-c_R\|\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\] is therefore valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz cones centered at sampled points lie below the objective. Their upper envelope and its regional infimum give a valid lower bound; a single sample yields the corresponding covering-radius bound.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz under \(\|\cdot\|\).
\(R\subseteq D\) is nonempty and compact.
\(S_R\subseteq R\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_R\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Longest-edge bisection of axis-aligned boxes with lower-bound-driven selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact box, let \(f:R_0\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Maintain a finite family \(\mathcal A_k\) of active axis-aligned boxes and, for every \(R\in\mathcal A_k\), a valid bound \(B_R\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\). Let \(U_k\) be the least objective value observed at sampled feasible points. Select a box attaining \(\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}B_R\), bisect one of its longest coordinate intervals at its midpoint, compute the samples and bounds required for the two children, update \(U_k\), and remove every box satisfying \(B_R>U_k\). Stop when \[U_k-\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}B_R\le\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain valid lower bounds on active rectangles, bisect a least-bound rectangle along a longest side, update sampled values and bounds, prune rectangles that cannot improve the incumbent, and stop when the global bound gap meets the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(R_0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty compact axis-aligned box.
Every active box \(R\) has a valid bound \(B_R\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\).
The active boxes cover every point not eliminated by a valid pruning test.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(U_k-\inf_{x\in R_0}f(x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on box R

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Longest-edge bisection of simplices in a bound-driven partition search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a compact polytope \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) have a finite simplicial decomposition with pairwise disjoint interiors, let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Maintain an active simplicial partition \(\mathcal A_k\), a valid bound \(B_S\le\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\) for each \(S\in\mathcal A_k\), and the least sampled value \(U_k\). Select a simplex attaining \(\min_{S\in\mathcal A_k}B_S\), choose one of its longest edges, insert the edge midpoint, and replace the selected simplex by the two simplices formed by that bisection. Update samples, bounds, and \(U_k\), and remove every simplex satisfying \(B_S>U_k\). Stop when \[U_k-\min_{S\in\mathcal A_k}B_S\le\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain valid lower bounds on an active simplicial partition, bisect a least-bound simplex across a longest edge, update samples and bounds, prune simplices that cannot improve the incumbent, and stop when the global bound gap meets the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a compact polytope with a finite simplicial decomposition.
Every active simplex \(S\) has a valid bound \(B_S\le\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\).
Bisection preserves coverage; conformity is enforced when required.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every refinement preserves coverage of \(D\), and termination implies \(U_k-\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on simplex S
