knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial partition of a compact star-shaped set into truncated conical regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and star-shaped with center \(c\). Represent active regions as truncated cones 	o\[R(c,V,[\alpha,	o\beta])=\{c+t(v-c):v\in V,	o\alpha\le t\le\beta\}\cap D,\] where \(V\) is a compact angular base. Select a region of least valid lower bound and subdivide either its radial interval or its angular base into finitely many children whose union is the parent. Update samples, bounds, and the incumbent, prune dominated children, and stop when the global bound gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).

Every conical region has a valid lower bound.
Infinite refinement makes both radial and angular diameters vanish.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposable Partition Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive finite decomposition operator for region-based global search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be a class of nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). A decomposable partition operator is a map \(\Pi\) assigning to each \(R\in\mathcal R\) a finite nonempty family \(\Pi(R)\subseteq\mathcal R\) such that \[R=\bigcup_{Q\in\Pi(R)}Q,\qquad \operatorname{int}(Q)\cap\operatorname{int}(Q')=\varnothing\quad(Q,Q'\in\Pi(R),\ Q\ne Q').\] It is exhaustive if every sequence satisfying \(R_{k+1}\in\Pi(R_k)\) also satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposable partition operator replaces each admissible compact region by finitely many interior-disjoint children covering it. It is exhaustive when the diameters in every infinite nested child sequence tend to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is a class of nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing any active region \(R\) by \(\Pi(R)\) preserves coverage, and exhaustive recursive decompositions have vanishing diameter along every infinite branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Objective Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McShane–Whitney extension theorem for a real-valued Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty subset of a metric space \((X,d)\), and let \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz. Define, for every \(x\in X\), \[F(x)=\inf_{s\in S}\bigl(f(s)+Ld(x,s)\bigr),\qquad G(x)=\sup_{s\in S}\bigl(f(s)-Ld(x,s)\bigr).\] Then \(F\) and \(G\) are \(L\)-Lipschitz extensions of \(f\). Moreover, every \(L\)-Lipschitz extension \(H:X\to\mathbb{R}\) of \(f\) satisfies \[G(x)\le H(x)\le F(x)\qquad(x\in X).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued Lipschitz function on a nonempty subset of a metric space has explicit lower and upper Lipschitz extensions to the whole space without increasing its Lipschitz constant. Every extension with that constant lies between these envelopes.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space.
\(S\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
\(f:S\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F|_S=G|_S=f\), both \(F\) and \(G\) are \(L\)-Lipschitz, and \(G\le H\le F\) for every \(L\)-Lipschitz extension \(H:X\to\mathbb{R}\) of \(f\).

notation.meaning: upper McShane envelope defined by the infimum formula
lower Whitney envelope defined by the supremum formula

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^q\). A linearly constrained feasible set is
\[
F=X\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}.
\]
The set \(F\) is compact. If \(X\) is polyhedral, then \(F\) is also polyhedral. A constrained partition search minimizes the objective only over \(F\), and a partition cell \(R\subseteq X\) is feasible precisely when \(R\cap F\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear inequalities and equalities cut a compact feasible set from the compact search domain. The feasible set is polyhedral when the search domain is polyhedral, and partition cells are relevant only when they intersect it.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained Feasible Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. Given convex functions \(g_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and affine functions \(h_j:X\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,q\), define
\[
F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0\ \text{for every }i,\ h_j(x)=0\ \text{for every }j\}.
\]
Then \(F\) is convex. If all \(g_i\) and \(h_j\) are continuous, then \(F\) is closed in \(X\), hence compact. Nonemptiness is an additional feasibility requirement and does not follow from convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex nonlinear inequalities and affine equalities define a convex feasible set; continuity makes it compact inside a compact domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonempty set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is star-shaped with respect to \(c\in F\) if
\[
(1-t)c+tx\in F\qquad\text{for every }x\in F\text{ and }t\in[0,1].
\]
Equivalently, every segment \([c,x]\) joining \(c\) to a feasible point lies entirely in \(F\). The kernel is
\[
\operatorname{ker}(F)=\{c\in F:[c,x]\subseteq F\text{ for every }x\in F\},
\]
and \(F\) is star-shaped exactly when \(\operatorname{ker}(F)\ne\varnothing\). Every nonempty convex set is star-shaped with every feasible point as a center, but the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible set is star-shaped when one feasible center sees every other feasible point along a segment contained entirely in the set.
knowledge_statements.title: Star-Shaped Feasible Sets

children.title: Feasible-Region Branching
children.top_down_role: Subdivision structures adapted to regions containing feasible candidates.

assumptions_latex: The current region \(R\) is compact and satisfies \(R\cap F\ne\varnothing\).
A finite partition rule produces compact children whose union is \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained children cover \(R\cap F\), so branching cannot discard a feasible global minimizer in \(R\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an active compact region \(R\) with \(R\cap F\ne\varnothing\), generate finitely many compact children \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) satisfying
\[
R=\bigcup_{j=1}^kR_j.
\]
Test each child for feasibility or obtain a certified infeasibility decision. Replace \(R\) in the active collection \(\mathcal A\) by precisely those children not certified infeasible. The required preservation condition is
\[
R\cap F=\bigcup_{j=1}^k(R_j\cap F).
\]
Continue until the selected active region satisfies the prescribed diameter, bound-gap, or global stopping tolerance, and return the best feasible sampled point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition a feasible parent, discard only children certified infeasible, and retain the remaining children; their feasible portions still cover the parent's feasible portion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\subseteq X\) be compact, let \(y\in R\cap F\), and suppose \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(|f(x)-f(z)|\le L\|x-z\|\) for all \(x,z\in F\). Define
\[
B_F(R)=f(y)-L\sup_{x\in R\cap F}\|x-y\|.
\]
Then
\[
B_F(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x).
\]
Replacing the feasible radius by any certified upper bound on it gives a possibly weaker but still valid regional lower certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible sample and an upper bound on its maximum distance to feasible points yield a certified Lipschitz lower bound for the region.

children.title: Infeasible Region Pruning
children.top_down_role: Exclusion of regions certified to contain no feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: A regional constraint certificate proves \(R\cap F=\varnothing\).
Only feasible points can solve the constrained optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting \(R\) from the active collection preserves the constrained global optimum and every feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound pruning predicates based solely on certified regional infeasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose feasibility is described by \(g_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\). A region \(R\) may be pruned when certified bounds imply at least one of
\[
\underline g_i(R)>0,\qquad \underline h_j(R)>0,\qquad\text{or}\qquad \overline h_j(R)<0,
\]
where \(\underline g_i(R)\le g_i(x)\) and \(\underline h_j(R)\le h_j(x)\le\overline h_j(R)\) for every \(x\in R\). Each predicate proves \(R\cap F=\varnothing\). Consequently, removing \(R\) cannot remove a feasible point or change \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Failure to certify infeasibility is inconclusive and does not justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a region only when rigorous constraint bounds prove it contains no feasible point; an inconclusive test must leave the region active.

assumptions_latex: Every parent is covered by its children, and only certified-infeasible regions are discarded.
Each regional lower bound is valid on the feasible portion of its region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity theorem for constrained Lipschitz tree-search extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. Consider a tree search whose children cover each parent, which discards only regions certified disjoint from \(F\), and whose bound satisfies
\[
B(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x)
\]
whenever \(R\cap F\ne\varnothing\). Assume every infinite retained branch has diameters tending to zero and that its bounds converge to the objective value at any common limit point. If selection is exhaustive among regions whose lower bounds can improve the incumbent, then incumbent values converge to \(f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\); every incumbent accumulation point with limiting value \(f^*\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage, sound pruning, valid lower bounds, shrinking retained branches, and exhaustive selection together make the constrained tree-search extension globally convergent.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Extension Validity

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is nonempty and compact.
The objective and constraint functions possess known Lipschitz constants on the search domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns a feasible incumbent \(x_\varepsilon\) with \(f(x_\varepsilon)\le f^*+\varepsilon\) once its certified global gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).

active partition and regional lower bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract partition-and-bound template pending identification of the precise Thach–Tuy variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize an active partition \(\mathcal A=\{X\}\) and a feasible incumbent value \(U=f(x^I)\). For each \(R\in\mathcal A\), use Lipschitz minorants of the objective and constraints to compute a valid lower bound \(B(R)\) over \(R\cap F\), assigning \(B(R)=+\infty\) when infeasibility is certified. Select a region of smallest bound, partition it, update \(U\) from newly obtained feasible points, and remove every region satisfying \(B(R)\ge U\). Stop when
\[
U-\min_{R\in\mathcal A}B(R)\le\varepsilon,
\]
and output its incumbent \(x_\varepsilon\). Then \(f(x_\varepsilon)\le f^*+\varepsilon\), provided the regional certificates and exhaustive refinement assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This provisional template partitions the domain, bounds objective and constraints by Lipschitz minorants, prunes dominated regions, and stops at a certified optimality gap.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a generic partition-and-bound template rather than an identifiable Thach–Tuy algorithm. A source is required to determine the intended variant, its regional certificates, update rules, and termination guarantee.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f\) and constraints \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are Lipschitz on a compact domain.
Each active region admits simultaneous valid lower bounds for all these functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint constraint bounds certify infeasibility, while the objective bound certifies whether a feasible region can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic joint objective-and-constraint bounding within each partition region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every active compact region \(R\), compute bounds satisfying
\[
B_f(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x),\qquad B_i(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}g_i(x),
\]
using common regional samples and valid Lipschitz constants. If \(B_i(R)>0\) for some \(i\), certify \(R\cap F=\varnothing\) and prune \(R\). Otherwise retain \(R\) unless \(B_f(R)\ge U\), where \(U\) is the best feasible objective value observed. Select and subdivide a retained region of smallest objective lower bound, update all bounds and \(U\), and stop when the incumbent-to-global-lower-bound gap meets the prescribed tolerance. Bounds alone never establish feasibility unless an actual feasible point or a separate feasibility certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound the objective and every constraint together; constraint bounds remove infeasible regions, while the objective bound removes regions unable to beat the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Constraint-Bounding Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic joint-bounding logic is plausible, but no source identifies the exact simultaneous constraint-bounding method, its sampling rule, or its convergence conditions. The named leaf therefore requires authoritative algorithm-level support.

assumptions_latex: The compact-domain problem is \(\min\{f(x):g_i(x)\le0\}\), with all functions Lipschitz.
A multiplier vector \(\lambda\ge0\) and penalty parameter \(\rho>0\) are fixed during each global subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Lipschitz global search can minimize the penalized function \(P_{\lambda,\rho}\); equivalence with the constrained problem requires an exact-penalty condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz global minimization of an inequality-violation penalty with multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), define
\[
P_{\lambda,\rho}(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\max\{0,g_i(x)\},
\]
where \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\rho>0\). Compute a valid Lipschitz constant for \(P_{\lambda,\rho}\), globally minimize it by partition search, update \(\lambda\) and \(\rho\) according to the observed violations, and retain the best feasible point. A minimizer of \(P_{\lambda,\rho}\) solves the constrained problem only when an applicable exact-penalty theorem ensures feasibility and objective equivalence; without that condition, penalized minimization is merely a relaxation procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine the objective, multiplier terms, and constraint violations into a Lipschitz penalty, solve successive global subproblems, and require exactness before claiming constrained optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Multiplier Lipschitz Methods

notation.meaning: global lower and incumbent upper bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence under uniformly shrinking cells and consistent regional bounds.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a finite partition of \(X\), with valid bounds \(B(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\). Assume
\[
\max_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0
\]
and, for every nested chain \(R_k\ni x\) with shrinking diameter, \(B(R_k)\to f(x)\). Define \(L_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B(R)\), and let \(U_k\) be the best sampled value under a sampling rule dense along refined chains. Then
\[
L_k\to f^*,\qquad U_k\to f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all cells shrink regularly, lower bounds become locally exact, and sampling follows refinement, the global lower and incumbent upper bounds meet at the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Partition Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The citation concerns multivariate rectangular partition methods, while the statement claims convergence for general finite partitions. Nestedness, refinement structure, uniform bound consistency, and the meaning of sampling dense along refined chains are not stated precisely enough to support the theorem. The exact sourced theorem must be checked.

children.title: Necessary Partition Convergence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Structural requirements that any convergent partition search must satisfy.

assumptions_latex: The partition method is required to converge for every Lipschitz objective on a compact domain.
Regions can remain potentially optimal whenever their lower bounds do not exceed the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point that can be a unique Lipschitz minimizer must be approached by indefinitely refined retained regions with asymptotically exact lower bounds.

notation.meaning: compact search domain and target point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise refinement and bound-consistency requirements necessary for universal Lipschitz convergence.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.2 Sufficient and Necessary Convergence Conditions p. 64

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a partition method converges to the global minimum for every Lipschitz function on a compact set \(X\). For each \(x\in X\) that can occur as the unique minimizer of such a function, the method must admit retained regions \(R_k\ni x\) along an infinite refinement subsequence such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0.
\]
Moreover, any lower-bounding rule used to exclude regions must be asymptotically consistent along that sequence:
\[
B(R_k)-\inf_{y\in R_k}f(y)\to0.
\]
Otherwise one can construct a Lipschitz objective with a sufficiently localized strict minimum at \(x\) for which the method neither resolves the minimizing neighborhood nor distinguishes its bound, contradicting universal convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Universal convergence requires indefinite refinement near every possible strict minimizer and lower bounds that become exact on the resulting shrinking regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Partition Convergence Conditions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.2 Sufficient and Necessary Convergence Conditions p. 64

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Universal objective-value convergence alone does not, under the stated assumptions, imply indefinite retained-region refinement at every possible unique minimizer; the claim depends on the oracle model, stopping convention, and precise definition of convergence. The final sentence is also proof text. This formulation is not a valid necessary condition as stated.

children.title: Sufficient Partition Convergence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Partition properties supporting convergence guarantees.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
Each active region \(R\) has a sampled point, a valid lower bound \(B_k(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), and an incumbent value \(u_k\).
Every region satisfying \(B_k(R)\leq u_k\) indefinitely is refined along descendants whose diameters tend to zero, and the bound error vanishes with diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\to f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: lower bound assigned to region R at iteration k
best sampled objective value through iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic compact-domain partition search with valid, asymptotically tight regional bounds.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.2 Sufficient and Necessary Convergence Conditions p. 64

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k(x^*)\) denote an active region containing a global minimizer \(x^*\). Suppose persistent competitiveness forces refinement of every nested chain \((R_{k_j}(x^*))_j\) whose lower bounds do not exceed the incumbent. If \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{k_j}(x^*))\to0\) and \(0\leq f(x^*)-B_{k_j}(R_{k_j}(x^*))\to0\), then the incumbent sequence is nonincreasing, satisfies \(u_k\geq f(x^*)\), and eventually admits sampled values arbitrarily close to \(f(x^*)\). Consequently, \(u_k\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid bounds, persistent selection of competitive regions, shrinking minimizer-containing cells, and vanishing bound error suffice for convergence of the best sampled value to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Partition Convergence Conditions

children.title: Partition Convergence Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where necessary criteria also provide sufficient coverage.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and partitions are nested, exhaustive, and shape regular.
Every cell created at level \(k\) receives a sample whose distance from every point of that cell is at most a fixed multiple of its diameter.
Convergence is required uniformly over all real-valued Lipschitz functions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_k\to0\iff \overline{\{x_k:k\geq1\}}=X\iff u_k(f)\to\min_X f\) for every Lipschitz \(f\).

notation.meaning: maximum diameter of a level-k partition cell

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence in the exhaustive, shape-regular, universally quantified Lipschitz regime.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.2 Sufficient and Necessary Convergence Conditions p. 64

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exhaustive shape-regular partition sequence, let \(\Delta_k:=\max_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\). Under the stated sampling rule, the following are equivalent: \(\Delta_k\to0\); the sample set \(\{x_k:k\geq1\}\) is dense in \(X\); and, for every Lipschitz function \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), the incumbent \(u_k(f):=\min_{1\leq i\leq k}f(x_i)\) converges to \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). The equivalence concerns universal convergence, not convergence for one fixed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exhaustive regular partitions, vanishing global mesh, dense sampling, and convergence for every Lipschitz objective are equivalent.

The cited locator has not been inspected sufficiently to confirm that the stated nesting, sampling, and shape-regularity assumptions establish this direction.

children.title: Necessity–Sufficiency Gaps
children.top_down_role: Settings where available necessary criteria do not establish convergence.

assumptions_latex: The feasible domain is \(X=[0,1]\).
The algorithm samples \(x_k=1/k\) and may refine only intervals containing these samples.
The objective is \(f(x)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k=1/k\to0=\min_X f\), although \(\overline{\{x_k:k\geq1\}}\neq X\).

notation.meaning: best sampled objective value through iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates objective-specific convergence from universal convergence criteria.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.2 Sufficient and Necessary Convergence Conditions p. 64

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The samples \(x_k=1/k\) are not dense in \(X=[0,1]\), and the diameters of regions away from zero need not decrease. Nevertheless, for the Lipschitz objective \(f(x)=x\), the incumbent satisfies \(u_k:=\min_{1\leq i\leq k}f(x_i)=1/k\to0=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). Thus density and global mesh decay, while necessary for convergence uniformly over all Lipschitz objectives in standard equivalence regimes, are not necessary for convergence on an individual objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search concentrating near zero converges for f(x)=x without dense sampling, exposing the gap between instance-specific necessity and universal sufficient conditions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact axis-aligned box and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
Each partition consists of closed axis-aligned rectangles with disjoint interiors.
Every rectangle that remains potentially optimal is repeatedly subdivided, and its descendant diameters tend to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a global minimizer and let \(R_{k_j}\in\mathcal P_{k_j}\) be nested rectangles containing \(x^*\) that are selected infinitely often. If \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{k_j})\to0\) and each selected rectangle receives a sample \(x_{R_{k_j}}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x_{R_{k_j}},R_{k_j})=0\) with sampling displacement controlled by \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{k_j})\), then \(x_{R_{k_j}}\to x^*\). Continuity gives \(f(x_{R_{k_j}})\to f(x^*)\), hence the incumbent values converge to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly refining a minimizer-containing chain of rectangles to zero diameter, with samples inside those rectangles, makes incumbent values converge globally.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Partition Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested simplicial refinement with an explicit diameter-contraction condition on a compact feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\in X\) be a global minimizer of \(f\), and let \((S_j)_{j\geq1}\) be a nested sequence of selected simplices satisfying \(x^*\in S_j\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(S_j)\to0\). If processing \(S_j\) produces a sample \(y_j\in S_j\), then \(y_j\to x^*\), \(f(y_j)\to f(x^*)\), and the best-sample incumbent satisfies \(u_k\to f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If selected simplices containing a global minimizer shrink to zero diameter and are sampled internally, their samples approach the minimizer and the incumbent converges to the global minimum.

\((\mathcal T_k)_{k\geq1}\) is a sequence of finite simplicial partitions of \(X\).
A nested sequence of selected simplices \((S_j)_{j\geq1}\) contains a global minimizer, satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(S_j)\to0\), and supplies samples \(y_j\in S_j\).
\(u_k\) is the smallest objective value sampled through iteration \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Consistency Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence driven by valid, uniformly consistent regional lower bounds and internal sampling of selected regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k:=\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}B_k(R)\). Suppose every selected region minimizes the active lower bounds, every resulting nested selected chain has diameter tending to zero, and each selected region is sampled internally. If the regional bounds are valid and satisfy the stated uniform consistency estimate, then \(L_k\to f^*\) and \(u_k\to f^*\), where \(f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When minimum-bound regions are refined to zero diameter, sampled internally, and equipped with valid bounds whose errors vanish uniformly with diameter, both the active global lower bound and the incumbent converge to the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
At iteration \(k\), \(\mathcal A_k\) is a finite active partition of \(X\), and each \(R\in\mathcal A_k\) has a bound \(B_k(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\).
There is a function \(\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) with \(\eta(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) such that \(0\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)-B_k(R)\leq\eta(\operatorname{diam}R)\).
A region attaining \(\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}B_k(R)\) is selected, every nested selected descendant chain has diameter tending to zero, and processing a selected region produces a sample inside it.
\(u_k\) is the smallest objective value sampled through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}B_k(R)\to f^*\) and \(u_k\to f^*\), where \(f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: best sampled objective value through iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Global Sample-Slope Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic maximum pairwise-slope estimator from all available samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\geq2\) distinct samples, define \[\widehat L_m:=\max_{1\leq i<j\leq m}\frac{|f_i-f_j|}{\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert}.\] If \(f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz, then \(0\leq\widehat L_m\leq L\), and adding a sample gives \(\widehat L_{m+1}\geq\widehat L_m\). The observed maximum is not, without an additional safeguard, a certified upper bound on the smallest valid Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global estimate is the largest observed pairwise slope. It is nondecreasing as samples are added and does not exceed a valid global Lipschitz constant, so it is not automatically a certified upper estimate.
assumptions_latex: Distinct sample points \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and values \(f_i=f(x_i)\) are available, with \(m\geq2\).
The norm used in every slope ratio is fixed.
For the comparison property, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\widehat L_m\leq L\) and \(\widehat L_{m+1}\geq\widehat L_m\).

notation.meaning: sample point and its objective value
valid global Lipschitz constant used for comparison

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2 Estimation of Lipschitzian Problem Characteristics in Global Optimization p. 155

assumptions_latex: \(R\subset X\) contains at least two distinct sampled points.
A fixed norm is used for distances.
For comparison, \(f\) has local Lipschitz constant \(L_R\) on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\widehat L(R)\leq L_R\), with \(\widehat L(R)\) determined only by samples in \(R\).

notation.meaning: sample indices whose points lie in R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local pairwise-slope estimate restricted to samples lying in one region.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.2 Subset-Specific Estimates of Lipschitzian Characteristics p. 157

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I_R:=\{i:x_i\in R\}\) with \(|I_R|\geq2\), define \[\widehat L(R):=\max_{i,j\in I_R,\ i<j}\frac{|f(x_i)-f(x_j)|}{\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert}.\] If \(f\) is \(L_R\)-Lipschitz on \(R\), then \(\widehat L(R)\leq L_R\). This estimate can be smaller than the global sample-slope estimate because it excludes cross-region pairs. For regions with fewer than two samples, a global estimate or prescribed positive safeguard must replace the undefined local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional characteristic is the largest pairwise slope among samples inside that region; sparse regions require a global or prescribed fallback.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz under a fixed norm.
Samples \((x_i,f_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq m\), are exact.
\(R\subset X\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_m(R):=\min_{x\in R}\ell_m(x)\leq\min_{x\in R}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound over region R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: McShane-type lower envelope and its induced regional lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.3 Bounding Procedures on the Basis of Sample Points p. 158

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the sample-point lower envelope by \[\ell_m(x):=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\bigl\{f_i-L\lVert x-x_i\rVert\bigr\}.\] Lipschitz continuity gives \(f(x)\geq f_i-L\lVert x-x_i\rVert\) for every \(i\), hence \(f(x)\geq\ell_m(x)\) throughout \(X\). For a compact region \(R\), the quantity \(B_m(R):=\min_{x\in R}\ell_m(x)\) is therefore a valid lower bound on \(\min_{x\in R}f(x)\). Adding samples can only increase \(\ell_m\) and \(B_m(R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz cones erected below exact sample values form a lower envelope; minimizing that envelope over a region yields a certified regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Point Bounding Procedures

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Order-Statistic Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-endpoint extrapolation from the largest observed sample slopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the observed slopes as \(S_{1:m}\leq\cdots\leq S_{m:m}\), choose \(k\) with \(1<k<m\), and set \(t:=S_{m-k:m}\). Fit a generalized Pareto model to the \(k\) excesses \(S_{m-k+j:m}-t\), \(1\leq j\leq k\). If the fitted parameters satisfy \(\widehat\xi<0\) and \(\widehat\beta>0\), return \(\widehat L_{m,k}:=t-\widehat\beta/\widehat\xi\); if \(\widehat\xi\geq0\), return no finite-endpoint estimate. The returned value is a statistical estimate, not a deterministic Lipschitz certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a generalized Pareto model to the largest observed slopes and, only under a negative fitted shape, extrapolate its finite endpoint; the result is not a deterministic upper-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: Observed slope statistics \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) are modeled as observations from a distribution with a finite upper endpoint.
An integer \(k\) satisfies \(1<k<m\).
A generalized Pareto model with fitted shape \(\widehat\xi\) and scale \(\widehat\beta>0\) is fitted above the threshold \(S_{m-k:m}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\widehat\xi<0\), then \(\widehat L_{m,k}:=S_{m-k:m}-\widehat\beta/\widehat\xi\); if \(\widehat\xi\geq0\), no finite-endpoint estimate is returned.

notation.meaning: r-th order statistic of the observed slopes
fitted generalized Pareto shape and scale

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Regional Characteristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive regional lower characteristic built from nonempty regional samples and safeguarded local slope information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a region \(R\) with \(I_k(R)\neq\varnothing\), choose \(\widetilde L_k(R):=\max\{\widehat L_k(R),L_k^{\mathrm{floor}}\}>0\) and define \[C_k(R):=\min_{x\in R}\max_{i\in I_k(R)}\bigl\{f(x_i)-\widetilde L_k(R)\lVert x-x_i\rVert\bigr\}.\] If \(\widetilde L_k(R)\) is at least a Lipschitz constant of \(f\) on \(R\), then \(C_k(R)\leq\min_{x\in R}f(x)\); otherwise \(C_k(R)\) is only a heuristic selection score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a region containing samples, the adaptive characteristic is the minimum of their safeguarded lower-cone envelope. It is a certified regional lower bound only when the safeguarded slope dominates a valid local Lipschitz constant.
assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the nonempty compact region \(R\) contains exact samples indexed by a nonempty set \(I_k(R)\).
The safeguarded value \(\widetilde L_k(R):=\max\{\widehat L_k(R),L_k^{\mathrm{floor}}\}\) is positive.
For certified use, \(f\) is Lipschitz on \(R\) and \(\widetilde L_k(R)\) is at least a valid Lipschitz constant of \(f\) on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_k(R)\leq\min_{x\in R}f(x)\) under the certified-use assumption.

notation.meaning: nonempty set of indices of samples lying in R

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Bound-Driven Region Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-characteristic-driven region selection with an explicit exploration safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a greedy iteration \(k\), form \(\mathcal E_k:=\{R\in\mathcal A_k:C_k(R)\leq u_k-\tau_k\}\). If \(\mathcal E_k\neq\varnothing\), choose \(R_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal E_k}C_k(R)\); otherwise choose \(R_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal A_k}C_k(R)\). At a scheduled exploration iteration, instead choose a longest-waiting region among those not eliminated by valid bounds. Refine \(R_k\), evaluate the prescribed child samples, update the incumbent and affected characteristics, and retain the other active regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On greedy iterations, select the eligible region with the smallest characteristic, falling back to the smallest characteristic over all active regions. On exploration iterations, refine a longest-waiting region that valid bounds have not eliminated.
assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the active set \(\mathcal A_k\) is finite and nonempty, and every \(R\in\mathcal A_k\) has a real-valued characteristic \(C_k(R)\).
The incumbent \(u_k\) and tolerance \(\tau_k\geq0\) are defined.
A prescribed schedule identifies exploration iterations and guarantees eventual reconsideration of every region not eliminated by valid bounds.
A tie-breaking rule is prescribed whenever an argmin or longest-waiting choice is not unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On greedy iterations, \(R_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal E_k}C_k(R)\) when \(\mathcal E_k\neq\varnothing\), and \(R_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal A_k}C_k(R)\) otherwise; scheduled exploration iterations use the stated override.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(u_0=\min_{R\in\mathcal P_0}f(x_R)\). At iteration \(k\), select a nonempty set \(S_k\subseteq\arg\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B_k(R)\), possibly augmented by safeguard regions. Replace every \(R\in S_k\) by finitely many children whose interiors are disjoint, whose union is \(R\), and whose maximum diameter is at most \(q\operatorname{diam}(R)\) for a fixed \(q\in(0,1)\). Evaluate \(f\) at required new representative points, retain all other regions, recompute their characteristics, and set \(u_{k+1}\) equal to the least value sampled through iteration \(k+1\). Stop when \(u_{k+1}-\min_{R\in\mathcal P_{k+1}}B_{k+1}(R)\leq\varepsilon\), when the selected diameter is below tolerance, or when the evaluation budget is exhausted.

assumptions_latex: \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluated exactly and is Lipschitz continuous with an unknown finite constant.
At iteration \(k\), the sampled points satisfy \(a=x_0<\cdots<x_k=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method adaptively constructs a positive slope estimate and samples the interval with the smallest induced Lipschitz lower characteristic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate Strongin-type unknown-Lipschitz-constant interval method.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Convergence of Univariate Global Optimization Algorithms p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(M_k=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}|z_i-z_{i-1}|/(x_i-x_{i-1})\) and choose \(m_k=rM_k\) when \(M_k>0\), using a fixed positive fallback otherwise. For each interval define \(B_i=(z_{i-1}+z_i)/2-m_k(x_i-x_{i-1})/4-(z_i-z_{i-1})^2/[4m_k(x_i-x_{i-1})]\). Choose \(t\in\arg\min_i B_i\) and evaluate at \(x_{k+1}=(x_{t-1}+x_t)/2-(z_t-z_{t-1})/(2m_k)\), clipped to the open interval if required numerically. Reorder the samples and repeat until the selected interval, evaluation budget, or incumbent-bound gap meets its stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the unknown slope from observed divided differences, score every interval by a Lipschitz lower value, and sample the interval with the smallest score.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongin Unknown-Constant Method

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.1 Convergence of Univariate Global Optimization Algorithms p. 75

assumptions_latex: \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\) is observed sequentially at ordered trial points.
A specified information model assigns each unsampled interval a conditional merit derived from the available observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting the interval of greatest information merit converts the observation model into a sequential global-search rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract information-based family; the intended deterministic or probabilistic model is unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given information \(\mathcal I_k=\{(x_i,f(x_i)):0\leq i\leq k\}\), assign every current interval \(I\in\mathscr I_k\) a model-specific quantity \(J_k(I)\) measuring its conditional potential to contain an objective value below the incumbent. Select \(I_k\in\arg\max_{I\in\mathscr I_k}J_k(I)\), place the next trial at the model-prescribed point inside \(I_k\), and update \(\mathcal I_{k+1}\). The merit, trial location, and convergence claim are meaningful only after specifying the information model; they must not be inferred solely from the phrase “information method.”
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An information method scores unsampled intervals using a specified observation model, then samples where the conditional potential for improvement is greatest.
knowledge_statements.title: Information Global Optimization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly warns that an information model must be specified, but no source is cited and the deterministic or probabilistic model defining the merit and trial location remains unresolved. The exact mathematical content therefore cannot yet be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Local Tuning Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods that adapt regional characteristics while retaining explicit global-search controls.

assumptions_latex: \(R\subset D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contains at least two sampled points.
A global nonnegative scale estimate \(M_k\) and a positive floor \(\eta_k\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(R)\) is positive, uses regional variation when informative, and cannot fall below the prescribed global or numerical floor.

notation.meaning: sampled points associated with region R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A safeguarded regional slope estimator for local partition characteristics.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the observed regional slope by \(L_k(R)=\max\{|f(x)-f(y)|/\|x-y\|:x,y\in X_k(R),\ x\neq y\}\). For a reliability multiplier \(r>1\), a global coupling coefficient \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\), and floor \(\eta_k>0\), define the regional working estimate by \(m_k(R)=\max\{rL_k(R),\alpha_kM_k,\eta_k\}\). A regional Lipschitz characteristic then substitutes \(m_k(R)\) for a single global constant when constructing the lower score of \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate slope from samples in each region, multiply for reliability, and enforce global and numerical floors before constructing that region's lower score.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Lipschitz Tuning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

assumptions_latex: Each region \(R\in\mathcal P_k\) has a global estimate \(M_k>0\) and a local estimate \(L_k(R)\geq0\).
A deterministic evidence predicate \(E_k(R)\) is fixed before region selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The characteristic uses local tuning only where the declared evidence predicate holds and otherwise reverts to the global scale.

notation.meaning: evidence that local tuning is admissible

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic switching between local and global Lipschitz scales.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose constants \(r_g>1\), \(r_\ell>1\), and \(\eta>0\). For every \(R\in\mathcal P_k\), evaluate a fixed evidence predicate \(E_k(R)\), such as requiring a prescribed number of distinct local samples and stability of recent local slopes. Set \(m_k(R)=\max\{r_\ell L_k(R),\eta\}\) when \(E_k(R)\) holds, and set \(m_k(R)=\max\{r_gM_k,\eta\}\) otherwise. Construct the region characteristic with \(m_k(R)\), select regions by that characteristic together with any global safeguard, and reevaluate \(E_k\) after refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a local slope only after a fixed evidence test passes; otherwise score the region with a conservative global slope estimate.
knowledge_statements.title: Global–Local Estimate Switching

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

assumptions_latex: \(L_k(R)\geq0\) is an observed regional slope and \(M_k\geq0\) is a global slope estimate.
The lower characteristic is monotone nonincreasing in its working Lipschitz scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Increasing reliability cannot raise the resulting lower characteristic, so larger reliability produces more conservative region bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability parameterization for conservative locally tuned characteristics.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r>1\), \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), and \(\eta>0\), define \(m_k(R;r)=\max\{rL_k(R),\alpha rM_k,\eta\}\). Reliability-controlled tuning requires that the same declared value of \(r\) be used in both estimation and region scoring, that \(m_k(R;r)>0\), and that any change of \(r\) occur by a predetermined rule independent of unseen objective values. If \(r_2\geq r_1>1\), then \(m_k(R;r_2)\geq m_k(R;r_1)\); hence any Lipschitz lower characteristic monotone in the scale is no larger at \(r_2\) than at \(r_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reliability multiplier inflates local and global slope estimates; increasing it makes compatible Lipschitz lower scores more conservative.
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability-Controlled Tuning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

assumptions_latex: \(D=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a box and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is sampled at endpoints of each active box diagonal.
Every selected box is split by a rule whose repeated application drives descendant diameters to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces endpoint-based locally tuned characteristics and refines a box minimizing that characteristic.

notation.meaning: opposite diagonal endpoints of box R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic rectangular diagonal method with region-dependent Lipschitz tuning.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97
2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(R\in\mathcal P_k\), evaluate any unevaluated endpoints \(a_R,b_R\), compute a safeguarded local scale \(m_k(R)>0\), and form the diagonal lower characteristic \(B_k(R)=[f(a_R)+f(b_R)-m_k(R)\|b_R-a_R\|]/2\). Select \(R_k\in\arg\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B_k(R)\), together with any safeguard choice. Split \(R_k\) along a longest coordinate or by the prescribed diagonal partition rule, reuse coincident endpoint evaluations, evaluate new diagonal endpoints, and update all affected local scales. Output the best sampled point when the bound gap, diameter tolerance, or evaluation budget is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each box from its diagonal endpoints and a local slope estimate, refine the lowest-scoring box, and reuse endpoint evaluations across descendants.
knowledge_statements.title: Locally Tuned Diagonal Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97
2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a multidimensional box, the displayed expression based only on two opposite endpoints is not generally a valid lower bound over the entire box, and standard diagonal methods use method-specific characteristics and partition rules. Because the candidate itself leaves the diagonal-characteristic variant unresolved, the exact formula and algorithm require direct source support before they can be accepted.

children.title: Adaptive Lipschitz Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families separating eventual bound validity, explicit global safeguards, and local-tuning guarantees.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
From some iteration \(K\), every active-region characteristic is a valid lower bound for \(f\) on that region.
A least-characteristic region is refined each iteration, and repeated refinement makes its descendant diameters vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values satisfy \(u_k\downarrow f^*=\min_{x\in D}f(x)\), and every accumulation point of improving trial points is globally minimizing.

notation.meaning: best value sampled by iteration k
iteration after which bounds are valid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence once all adaptive regional lower bounds eventually become valid.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59
2.2.1 Convergence of Branch-and-Bound Type Methods p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) for every \(k\geq K\) and every \(R\in\mathcal P_k\). Suppose a region attaining \(\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B_k(R)\) is refined, representative samples become dense along every infinitely refined nested chain, and the lower characteristic is consistent in the sense that \(u_k-B_k(R_k)\to0\) whenever \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\). Then \(\lim_{k\to\infty}u_k=f^*\). Any convergent subsequence of trial points whose objective values tend to \(f^*\) has its limit in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If adaptive regional scores eventually become valid and consistent lower bounds, repeated best-bound refinement drives incumbent values to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Bound-Validity Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59
2.2.1 Convergence of Branch-and-Bound Type Methods p. 35

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
The complete trial sequence \((x_k)_{k\geq0}\subset D\) contains a safeguard subsequence that is dense in \(D\).
The incumbent is \(u_k=\min_{0\leq j\leq k}f(x_j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\downarrow f^*=\min_{x\in D}f(x)\). Moreover, every accumulation point of a trial subsequence whose objective values converge to \(f^*\) is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value convergence supplied by a dense deterministic safeguard subsequence.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, and let \((x_k)_{k\geq0}\subset D\) be the complete trial sequence generated by the adaptive search and its safeguard. Define \(u_k=\min_{0\leq j\leq k}f(x_j)\) and \(f^*=\min_{x\in D}f(x)\). If the trial sequence contains a safeguard subsequence dense in \(D\), then \(u_k\downarrow f^*\). Every accumulation point of any subsequence \((x_{k_j})\) satisfying \(f(x_{k_j})\to f^*\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a compact domain, a dense safeguard subsequence guarantees convergence of the best observed value, regardless of the validity of adaptive local scores.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Safeguard Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
For every global minimizer \(x^*\), regions containing \(x^*\) are refined infinitely often and their diameters tend to zero.
Along those regions, tuned scales eventually dominate the true local Lipschitz modulus and their characteristics are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values converge to \(f^*\), and trial points generated in the shrinking minimizing regions have globally minimizing accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence of locally tuned search near every global minimizer.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131
2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)\). Suppose the algorithm generates a nested subsequence \(R_{k_j}(x^*)\ni x^*\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{k_j}(x^*))\to0\), samples a point \(y_j\in R_{k_j}(x^*)\), and eventually uses \(m_{k_j}(R_{k_j}(x^*))\) no smaller than the Lipschitz modulus of \(f\) on that region. Then \(|f(y_j)-f(x^*)|\leq L\operatorname{diam}(R_{k_j}(x^*))\to0\). Therefore the incumbents satisfy \(u_k\to f^*\). If the same conditions hold for every minimizer-relevant chain selected by the method, locally tuned characteristics preserve global value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local tuning converges when minimizer-containing regions keep shrinking and their tuned slopes eventually dominate the objective's local variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Tuning Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131
2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed argument obtains convergence solely by assuming that a minimizer-containing chain is already refined to zero diameter and sampled. It does not establish that locally tuned characteristics cause such refinement, while the eventual local-modulus condition is unused in the stated convergence implication. A method-specific selection rule and corresponding convergence theorem must be sourced before this can represent Local-Tuning Convergence.

children.title: Adaptive Estimation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by invalid learned bounds, sparse observations, unstable regional estimates, or premature localization.

assumptions_latex: The search uses regional working estimates \(m_k(R)\) to construct purported Lipschitz lower characteristics.
There exist an open set \(U\subset D\), a constant \(L_U>0\), and infinitely many relevant iterations with \(m_k(R)<L_U\) for regions \(R\subset U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The purported characteristics need not be lower bounds, and bound-only selection can permanently discard a region containing a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by indefinitely nonconservative regional slope estimates.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14
2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Persistent Lipschitz underestimation occurs when there are regions \(R_k\subset U\) at arbitrarily large iterations such that \(m_k(R_k)<L_U\), where \(L_U=\sup_{x\neq y\in U}|f(x)-f(y)|/\|x-y\|\). A characteristic derived by replacing \(L_U\) with \(m_k(R_k)\) is then not guaranteed to satisfy \(B_k(R_k)\leq\inf_{x\in R_k}f(x)\). In particular, a narrow unsampled well inside \(R_k\) may coexist with nearly flat sampled values, causing the computed score to exceed the true regional minimum. Without a global safeguard or eventual correction, bound-only selection may never refine that well and need not converge globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If regional slopes remain below true local variation, computed lower scores can exclude a narrow global well forever, so bound-only search may fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Lipschitz Underestimation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.4 Lipschitz Global Optimization p. 14
2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz continuous.
The sampled set \(S\subset X\) is finite and contains at least two distinct points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L(S)\le L_S\le L\), and the gap \(L-widehat L(S)\) can remain arbitrarily large for sparse \(S\).

notation.meaning: Empirical maximum pairwise slope on the sampled set
Smallest Lipschitz constant of the restriction of the objective to the sampled set
A valid global Lipschitz constant for the objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic downward bias of pairwise-slope estimation under geometrically sparse sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the empirical estimator \(\widehat L(S)=\max_{x,y\in S,\,x\ne y}|f(x)-f(y)|/\|x-y\|\), every valid global Lipschitz constant \(L\) satisfies \(\widehat L(S)\le L\). Sparse samples need not encounter regions of maximal slope: for any finite \(S\subset X\) and any \(M>0\), whenever \(X\setminus S\) contains a nonempty open ball, there exists a Lipschitz function agreeing with a constant on \(S\) whose global Lipschitz constant is at least \(M\). Thus sample consistency alone provides no nontrivial upper estimate of global regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum observed pairwise slope systematically misses unsampled steep regions; with finitely many sparse samples, the true Lipschitz constant can exceed the empirical estimate arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Sample Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated adversarial construction or estimator convention. The conclusion contains malformed LaTeX (`L-widehat L(S)`), and “global Lipschitz constant” must mean the least Lipschitz constant rather than an arbitrarily chosen valid upper bound. Source support and a precise corrected formulation are required.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), each active region \(R\) has a finite sample set \(S_{k,R}\) containing at least two distinct points.
Regional regularity is estimated by maximum observed pairwise slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small changes in regional membership or samples can produce unbounded relative changes in \(\widehat L_{k,R}\) when the previous estimate is zero or arbitrarily small.

notation.meaning: Active region and its samples at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of regionwise pairwise-slope estimates after adaptive repartitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\widehat L_{k,R}=\max_{x,y\in S_{k,R},\,x\ne y}|f(x)-f(y)|/\|x-y\|\). There is no uniform continuity bound for this estimator under insertion, deletion, or reassignment of a sample: two samples with equal values give \(\widehat L_{k,R}=0\), while adding a point at distance \(\delta>0\) with value difference \(a>0\) gives an estimate at least \(a/\delta\). Consequently, adaptive changes of region boundaries or sample membership can abruptly change regional regularity estimates even when all previously observed values remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regionwise slope estimates can jump from zero to an arbitrarily large value when repartitioning adds or reassigns a nearby sample with a different objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Estimate Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic match, but the claimed absence of a uniform continuity bound depends on what perturbations and objective class are held fixed. For a fixed globally Lipschitz objective, observed slopes are bounded by its Lipschitz constant. No cited source establishes the intended adaptive-region failure regime.

assumptions_latex: A partition search selects future regions only from descendants of a localized active family \(\mathcal A_k\).
The localization rule may discard regions using underestimated regularity bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a discarded region contains every global minimizer, then no subsequent iterate can approach the global minimum.

notation.meaning: Family of regions retained after iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irrecoverable loss of global convergence caused by nonexhaustive adaptive localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\), and suppose that after iteration \(k\) every future sample is restricted to \(U_k=\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal A_k}R\). If \(\overline{U_k}\cap X^*=\varnothing\), then compactness and continuity imply \(\inf_{x\in\overline{U_k}}f(x)>min_{x\in X}f(x)\). Hence the best objective values generated after localization remain separated from the global minimum. Any rule capable of permanently deleting a region solely because of an underestimated local Lipschitz constant therefore lacks a general global-convergence guarantee without an independent exhaustive exploration mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once localization permanently excludes all global minimizers, later samples cannot recover global optimality; exhaustive exploration or reliable bounds are therefore necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Localization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Premature exclusion is appropriately a failure boundary, but the strict objective gap requires compactness of the relevant closed set and continuity of the objective, neither of which appears in the assumptions. The statement also contains malformed `min` LaTeX. An algorithm-specific source is needed for the broader claim about deletion rules and global convergence.

children.title: DIRECT Algorithm
children.top_down_role: Canonical normalized-box method combining implicit Lipschitz-scale search, representative-point evaluation, and rectangular refinement.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(D=\prod_{j=1}^n[a_j,b_j]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(a_j<b_j\) for every \(j\).
\(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is an objective function that attains its minimum on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization over \(D\) is equivalent to optimization over \([0,1]^n\) under an invertible affine change of variables.

notation.meaning: Affine normalization from the unit cube to the original box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine unit-cube normalization used by box-based DIRECT search.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case, p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(T:[0,1]^n\to D\) by \(T(u)_j=a_j+(b_j-a_j)u_j\), and define \(g:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(g(u)=f(T(u))\). Then \(T\) is bijective, with \(T^{-1}(x)_j=(x_j-a_j)/(b_j-a_j)\). Consequently, \(\min_{x\in D}f(x)=\min_{u\in[0,1]^n}g(u)\), and \(u^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in[0,1]^n}g(u)\) if and only if \(T(u^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)\). Under this normalization, every axis-aligned subbox has dimensionless coordinate lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine bijection maps the original search box to the unit cube, preserving objective values and minimizers and giving subboxes dimensionless side lengths.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Box Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case, p. 39

assumptions_latex: The active rectangles are indexed by the finite set \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
Each \(R_i\) has sampled center value \(f_i\in\mathbb{R}\) and size \(d_i\ge 0\).
The incumbent is \(f_{\min}=\min_{j\in I}f_j\), and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rectangle is potentially optimal precisely when it minimizes \(f_i-Kd_i\) for at least one \(K>0\) and satisfies the stated sufficient-improvement condition at that same scale.

notation.meaning: Objective value sampled at the center of rectangle i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical DIRECT selection interpreted as simultaneous search over positive Lipschitz scales.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case, p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each hypothetical scale \(K>0\), associate with \(R_i\) the score \(f_i-Kd_i\). The rectangle \(R_i\) is potentially optimal when there exists \(K>0\) such that \(f_i-Kd_i\le f_j-Kd_j\) for every \(j\in I\) and \(f_i-Kd_i\le f_{\min}-\varepsilon|f_{\min}|\). DIRECT therefore searches implicitly over positive scales rather than fixing or estimating one Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DIRECT treats every positive hypothetical Lipschitz scale as possible and selects a rectangle when its size-adjusted center value is minimal at some scale and passes the sufficient-improvement test.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Lipschitz-Scale Search

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case, p. 39

assumptions_latex: The objective is evaluated at the center of every active axis-aligned rectangle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each active rectangle is summarized for selection by its center, center value, and a scalar radius.

notation.meaning: Center and sampled center value of rectangle i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite center-value-radius encoding of active DIRECT rectangles.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write an active rectangle as \(R_i=\prod_{j=1}^n[c_{ij}-h_{ij},c_{ij}+h_{ij}]\), where \(h_{ij}\ge0\), and sample \(f_i=f(c_i)\). Its Euclidean center-to-vertex radius is \(d_i=\|h_i\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^n h_{ij}^2)^{1/2}\). The triple \((c_i,f_i,d_i)\) supplies the geometric and objective information used in classical potentially-optimal selection: rectangles with identical \(d_i\) are compared by \(f_i\), while different sizes are compared through affine scores \(f_i-Kd_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DIRECT encodes each rectangle by its center, sampled center value, and center-to-vertex radius; these size-value pairs drive potentially optimal selection.
knowledge_statements.title: Center-Sampling Representation

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

assumptions_latex: \(R=\prod_{j=1}^n[c_j-h_j,c_j+h_j]\) is an active rectangle with \(h_j\ge 0\).
The maximal half-length \(H=\max_{1\le j\le n}h_j\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Processing every coordinate in \(I=\{j:h_j=H\}\) by the DIRECT trisection step produces axis-aligned children with pairwise disjoint interiors whose union is \(R\).

notation.meaning: Set of coordinates attaining the longest side length
One third of a longest full side length

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical longest-coordinate trisection step; the value-based processing order may vary by implementation.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case, p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(I=\{j:h_j=H\}\) and \(\delta=2H/3\). Evaluate any previously unsampled trial centers \(c-\delta e_j\) and \(c+\delta e_j\) for \(j\in I\). Process the coordinates in the algorithm's prescribed order and, for each processed coordinate \(j\), cut the current central rectangle at the two hyperplanes with coordinate values \(c_j-\delta/2\) and \(c_j+\delta/2\). After every coordinate in \(I\) has been processed, the resulting axis-aligned rectangles have pairwise disjoint interiors and union \(R\), and their sampled centers reuse the trial evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DIRECT samples offsets along every longest coordinate and successively trisects those coordinates, producing a partition of the selected rectangle while reusing the trial evaluations.
knowledge_statements.title: Longest-Side Rectangle Trisection
