Fixed absolute orientation tolerances can also produce order-dependent approximate hulls. The cited face/extreme-point section does not support this numerical policy.

children.title: Reusable Sample Identification
children.top_down_role: Recognition of previously evaluated points applicable to a current region or request.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Sample Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for reusing deterministic objective evaluations across partition regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), a requested evaluation at \(x\in X\) is reusable from a cached record \((x',y',\kappa')\) exactly when the canonical keys agree, \(\kappa(x)=\kappa'\), and the record belongs to the same objective version and evaluation configuration. Under exact keying, agreement implies \(x=x'\) and the reusable value is \(y'=f(x)\). If keying deliberately identifies nearby but unequal points, the returned value is an approximation rather than an exact reuse and requires a separately stated error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse a cached value only when canonical point, objective version, and evaluation configuration all match.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is deterministic under the recorded evaluation configuration.
\(\kappa:X\to K\) is the cache-key map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matching valid record supplies the exact value \(f(x)\) whenever \(\kappa\) is injective on evaluated points.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports cache identity and versioning semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, the opening “exactly when” criterion permits equal noninjective keys, while the later conclusion requires injectivity for exact reuse. The identity rule and version/configuration semantics need authoritative support and reconciliation.

children.title: Evaluation Cache Design
children.top_down_role: Storage organizations for objective, constraint, status, or metadata records.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation Cache Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical cache state for deterministic point evaluations and provenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the evaluation cache as a finite partial map \(C:K\rightharpoonup X\times\mathbb R\times M\), where \(K\) is the key space and \(M\) stores objective version, scaling convention, fidelity, and evaluation status. A successful insertion of an evaluation \((x,f(x),m)\) sets \(C(\kappa(x))=(x,f(x),m)\). A lookup at \(x\) is a hit only if \(C(\kappa(x))\) exists, its stored point satisfies the chosen identity rule, and its metadata is compatible with the request. Otherwise the objective is evaluated and a new record is inserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store each evaluation by a canonical point key together with its value and compatibility metadata.
assumptions_latex: Objective evaluations are deterministic within each metadata configuration.
Each completed record is immutable or versioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible repeated requests return one stored value without an additional objective evaluation.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the cache representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but no citation supports it. A partial map with one record per key also needs an explicit collision policy when distinct stored points share a key.

children.title: Cross-Region Sample Sharing
children.top_down_role: Reuse of common samples across adjacent, nested, or overlapping regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Region Sample Sharing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of sharing one point evaluation among overlapping partition regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_q\subseteq X\) be active regions and let an exactly cached sample satisfy \(y=f(x)\). The pair \((x,y)\) may be attached to every region \(R_j\) containing \(x\), without reevaluating \(f\). For any valid region lower-bound operator \(B(R,S)\) defined from a sample set \(S\), adding the shared sample preserves validity provided \(B\) uses only globally valid regularity information and samples lying in its declared admissible domain. Region-specific surrogate states or local regularity estimates may not be shared merely because the underlying point is shared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One exact evaluation may serve every region containing its point, but region-specific model state remains separate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is deterministic.
The cached sample is exact and configuration-compatible.
Each region bound uses only admissible samples and valid regularity data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sharing \((x,f(x))\) across all containing regions preserves the validity of their bound computations.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports cross-region reuse conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Exact deterministic values can be shared across containing regions, but the assumptions do not formally ensure that an arbitrary operator remains a valid lower bound after its sample set changes; monotonicity or validity for every admissible augmented sample set must be stated.

children.title: Cache Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity limits for cached results under changing evaluation conditions or problem state.

knowledge_statements.title: Cache Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circumstances under which cached objective values cease to be exact substitutes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached record \((x,y,m)\) is not an exact substitute for a requested evaluation whenever at least one of the following changes: the objective definition or data, fidelity, random seed semantics, constraint or penalty parameters, coordinate interpretation, arithmetic policy, or any other metadata component affecting the returned value. Likewise, tolerance-based key equality between distinct points \(x\ne x'\) does not justify exact reuse for a merely Lipschitz objective; it yields only \(|f(x)-f(x')|\le L\lVert x-x'\rVert\) when a valid constant \(L\) is known. Such records must be invalidated, version-separated, or treated as approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective, metadata, or coordinate changes invalidate exact cache reuse; nearby-point reuse requires an explicit error allowance.
assumptions_latex: Requested and cached evaluations may differ in point or evaluation metadata.
When invoked, \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in the stated norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact reuse is confined to identical points and value-determining configurations; otherwise invalidation or bounded approximation is required.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports cache invalidation boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the Lipschitz error formula is standard, but no source supports the asserted cache invalidation boundaries or their implementation semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Point Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical suppression of repeated trial points in partition-based search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the canonical-key set \(E=\{\kappa(x_i):x_i\text{ has been evaluated}\}\) and, optionally, a pending set \(P\). For each proposed trial point \(x\), evaluate it only if \(\kappa(x)\notin E\cup P\); otherwise return the compatible cached or pending record. Before dispatch, insert \(\kappa(x)\) into \(P\) atomically. After successful completion, remove it from \(P\), store the result, and insert it into \(E\). If a region repeatedly proposes an existing key, its trial-generation rule must select a different admissible point or declare that region exhausted under the keying resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track evaluated and pending canonical keys so each admissible point is dispatched at most once per configuration.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) is fixed for the current objective configuration.
Membership testing and pending-set insertion are atomic when evaluations run concurrently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No canonical key is simultaneously dispatched more than once, and completed duplicates reuse the stored result.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports duplicate-dispatch control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the topic, but no source is supplied. The pending-key lifecycle also omits cancellation or failed-evaluation cleanup, so the stated control mechanism is incomplete outside successful completion.

children.title: Domain Coordinate Normalization
children.top_down_role: Rescaling of feasible-domain coordinates to comparable numerical ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Coordinate Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine normalization of a bounded hyperrectangle to the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\) with \(u_j>\ell_j\), and set \(D=\operatorname{diag}(u_1-\ell_1,\ldots,u_n-\ell_n)\). The bijection \(x=\ell+Dz\) maps \([0,1]^n\) onto \(X\), with inverse \(z=D^{-1}(x-\ell)\). Define \(g(z)=f(\ell+Dz)\). Then \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=\min_{z\in[0,1]^n}g(z)\), and minimizers correspond through the affine map. If \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in a chosen norm, then \(g\) is at most \(L\lVert D\rVert\)-Lipschitz in the induced operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map each bounded coordinate interval affinely to the unit interval while preserving objective values and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\) and \(u_j>\ell_j\) for every \(j\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the original objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized problem on \([0,1]^n\) is optimization-equivalent to the original problem on \(X\).
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports coordinate normalization and Lipschitz transformation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine normalization, minimizer correspondence, and induced-norm Lipschitz bound are mathematically precise and the representation kind fits, but the record contains no inspectable citation.

children.title: Objective Magnitude Scaling
children.top_down_role: Rescaling of objective values or associated search characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Magnitude Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive affine objective scaling and its effect on bounds and regularity constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(a>0\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\), and define the scaled objective \(g(x)=(f(x)-b)/a\). Then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}g(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(\min_X g=(\min_X f-b)/a\). Every lower bound \(B\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) transforms to \((B-b)/a\le\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\). If \(f\) is \(L_f\)-Lipschitz, then \(g\) is \(L_f/a\)-Lipschitz. Consequently, objective values, lower bounds, tolerances, and regularity constants must all be converted using the same scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive affine objective scaling preserves minimizers while scaling values, bounds, tolerances, and Lipschitz constants consistently.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(a>0\), and \(b\in\mathbb R\).
All comparisons are transformed to one common objective scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive affine scaling preserves the optimization ordering and transforms certified bounds and Lipschitz constants by \(1/a\).

notation.meaning: valid regional lower bound for the original objective

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the complete scaling interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive affine scaling formulas are correct and the representation kind fits, but no source is supplied. “Tolerances” should be limited explicitly to objective-value or bound tolerances because coordinate and other tolerances do not generally scale by \(1/a\).

children.title: Anisotropic Variable Scaling
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-specific scaling for unequal sensitivities or domain widths.

knowledge_statements.title: Anisotropic Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal coordinate scaling with the corresponding weighted Lipschitz metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(s_j>0\), set \(x=c+Sz\), and define \(g(z)=f(c+Sz)\). If \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\lVert S^{-1}(x-y)\rVert\) on \(X\), then \(|g(z)-g(w)|\le L\lVert z-w\rVert\) on \(S^{-1}(X-c)\). Conversely, an \(L\)-Lipschitz bound for \(g\) induces the displayed weighted-metric bound for \(f\). Thus anisotropic scaling is equivalent to choosing a weighted norm, and all region diameters used in Lipschitz lower bounds must be measured in that same metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal variable scaling is equivalent to a weighted norm and requires region diameters and Lipschitz constants to use that norm.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
The same underlying norm is used before and after the coordinate map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate transformation preserves the Lipschitz inequality exactly when the original space uses the induced weighted metric.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports anisotropic metric equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-metric equivalence is mathematically coherent and the representation kind fits, but no source or locator supports it.

children.title: Scaling Sensitivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search behavior affected by poor, changing, or problem-dependent scaling choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Sensitivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity-bound distortion caused by ill-conditioned coordinate or objective scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=c+Sz\) with invertible diagonal \(S\), Euclidean Lipschitz constants satisfy \(L_g\le L_f\lVert S\rVert_2\) and \(L_f\le L_g\lVert S^{-1}\rVert_2\). Hence uncertainty in a scalar regularity estimate can be amplified by the condition number \(\kappa_2(S)=\lVert S\rVert_2\lVert S^{-1}\rVert_2\). Scaling is well-conditioned when \(\kappa_2(S)\) is moderate and objective scaling remains far from overflow, underflow, and comparison tolerance. In the sensitive regime of large \(\kappa_2(S)\) or extreme objective scale, isotropic bounds become loose and finite-precision ranking or stopping tests may change unless constants and tolerances are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large scaling condition numbers or extreme objective scales amplify bound uncertainty and can destabilize finite-precision decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g(z)=f(c+Sz)\) use Euclidean Lipschitz constants.
\(S\) is invertible and diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distortion between scalar Lipschitz descriptions is bounded by \(\kappa_2(S)\), identifying ill-conditioned scaling as a sensitivity boundary.

notation.meaning: Euclidean Lipschitz constants before and after scaling
Euclidean condition number of the scaling matrix

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the stated sensitivity regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the inequalities require \(L_f\) and \(L_g\) to mean minimal Lipschitz moduli or explicitly chosen compatible bounds. The uncertainty-amplification and finite-precision regime claims have no numerical-analysis source.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Region Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous batched evaluation for deterministic partition search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current partition \(\mathcal P_k\), scores computed from all observations available at iteration \(k\), and \(p\) workers, select a frozen batch \(B_k\subseteq\mathcal P_k\). Assign each region \(R\in B_k\) an unevaluated trial point \(x_R\in R\), evaluate the points concurrently, and wait until every returned value \(f(x_R)\) has been recorded. Then update the incumbent, region bounds, cache, and partition to obtain \(\mathcal P_{k+1}\). Stop when a certified global gap is at most \(\varepsilon\), or when the prescribed evaluation budget is exhausted. Parallel execution changes neither the batch's trial points nor its deterministic post-batch update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freeze a batch of prioritized regions, evaluate one new point per region concurrently, then update all bounds and partitions synchronously after the batch completes.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is evaluated without worker-dependent error.
Batch selection uses only observations available before the batch begins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{f(x_R):R\in B_k\}\) is incorporated atomically into the next partition state.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

review_flags: parallel scheduling specialization requires source confirmation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the implementation-mechanism leaf, and the synchronous frozen-batch protocol is internally coherent. However, the cited general Lipschitz-partition section does not specifically establish parallel scheduling, atomic batch incorporation, or invariance of trial points and updates under parallel execution. An inspectable parallel global-optimization source is required.

children.title: Method Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem characteristics separating certified Lipschitz search, adaptive estimation, DIRECT, and methods owned by neighboring chapters.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a compact metric space, and \(\mathcal P\) is a finite cover of \(X\).
The finite evaluated set is \(\{x_i:i\in I\}\subseteq X\), and each \(R\in\mathcal P\) is assigned a nonempty index set \(I_R\subseteq I\).
\(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq Ld(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\), where the valid constant \(L\geq0\) is known.
The requested tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\mathrm{UB}-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\mathrm{UB}-\mathrm{LB}\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for region R
nonempty sample-index set used for region R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-gap certificate using a valid known Lipschitz constant.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131
2.4 Lipschitz Continuity p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz on a compact metric space \((X,d)\), where the valid constant \(L\geq0\) is known. Let \(\{x_i:i\in I\}\) be a nonempty finite set of evaluated points. For each \(R\in\mathcal P\), choose a nonempty set \(I_R\subseteq I\) and define \(\ell_R=\max_{i\in I_R}\{f(x_i)-L\sup_{x\in R}d(x,x_i)\}\). Then \(\ell_R\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\). If the finite cover \(\mathcal P\) covers \(X\), define \(\mathrm{LB}=\min_{R\in\mathcal P}\ell_R\) and \(\mathrm{UB}=\min_{i\in I}f(x_i)\). For any \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the condition \(\mathrm{UB}-\mathrm{LB}\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that an evaluated incumbent attaining \(\mathrm{UB}\) is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact metric domain and a known valid Lipschitz constant, every nonempty selected set of evaluated samples supplies a valid lower bound for each covering region. If the best sampled value is within epsilon of the smallest regional lower bound, the sampled incumbent is globally epsilon-optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Constant Certified Route

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Partition Strategies in General Lipschitz Optimization p. 131
2.4 Lipschitz Continuity p. 51

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a compact metric space, and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is Lipschitz with finite unknown constant \(L_*\).
At iteration \(k\), the evaluated set is \(\{x_i:1\leq i\leq N_k\}\), and its fill distance \(h_k\) tends to zero.
There exist \(k_0\) and a finite \(\overline L\) such that \(L_*\leq\widehat L_k\leq\overline L\) for every \(k\geq k_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\mathrm{UB}_k-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\mathrm{UB}_k-\mathrm{LB}_k\leq(2L_*+\overline L)h_k\to0\) for \(k\geq k_0\), whereas a gap formed before validated domination remains provisional.

notation.meaning: adaptive Lipschitz estimate at iteration k
finite eventual upper bound on the adaptive estimates
fill distance of the evaluated points at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional assurance when an estimated Lipschitz constant replaces the unknown constant.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.4 Lipschitz-Constant Estimation, Using Results from Extreme Order Statistics p. 160
2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be Lipschitz on a compact metric space \((X,d)\) with finite unknown constant \(L_*\). At iteration \(k\), let \(x_1,\ldots,x_{N_k}\) be the evaluated points and define their fill distance by \(h_k=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{1\leq i\leq N_k}d(x,x_i)\). Using an adaptive estimate \(\widehat L_k\), define \(q_k(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq N_k}\{f(x_i)-\widehat L_kd(x,x_i)\}\), \(\mathrm{LB}_k=\inf_{x\in X}q_k(x)\), and \(\mathrm{UB}_k=\min_{1\leq i\leq N_k}f(x_i)\). If \(h_k\to0\) and there exist \(k_0\) and \(\overline L<\infty\) such that \(L_*\leq\widehat L_k\leq\overline L\) for every \(k\geq k_0\), then the later lower bounds are valid and \(\mathrm{UB}_k-\mathrm{LB}_k\to0\). Until domination of \(L_*\) has been independently validated, a gap computed with \(\widehat L_k\) is provisional and does not certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimated Lipschitz constant gives valid convergent gaps once it is known to dominate the true constant, remains uniformly bounded, and the evaluated points become dense. Before domination is validated, its computed gaps are only provisional.

2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Constant DIRECT Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potentially-optimal rectangle selection without fixing one Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For box-constrained minimization, maintain rectangles \(R_i\) with centers \(c_i\), center values \(f(c_i)\), and size measures \(d_i\). Declare \(R_j\) potentially optimal if some \(K>0\) satisfies \(f(c_j)-Kd_j\leq f(c_i)-Kd_i\) for every \(i\), together with \(f(c_j)-Kd_j\leq f_{\min}-\eta|f_{\min}|\). At each iteration, select all such rectangles, divide each along its longest coordinate directions, and evaluate the new subrectangle centers. Return the best sampled center when the budget or stopping rule is met. The existential slope \(K\) avoids committing to a known Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DIRECT selects rectangles that could be best for some positive Lipschitz slope, subdivides their longest dimensions, and retains the best sampled center.
assumptions_latex: \(f:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb R\) is evaluated at rectangle centers.
\(\eta\geq0\) is a prescribed sufficient-improvement parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected rectangles lie on the lower convex envelope of the points \((d_i,f(c_i))\) under the stated improvement test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the DIRECT-route leaf, and the stated potentially-optimal inequalities resemble the standard DIRECT selection rule. No citation is supplied, however, so the precise sufficient-improvement convention, rectangle-size definition, lower-hull characterization, and subdivision rule cannot be accepted as sourced candidate knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Expensive-Evaluation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallelism reduces elapsed batch time, not black-box sample complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a batch of \(m\) independent objective evaluations, each taking time \(\tau\), executed on \(p\) identical workers with negligible scheduling and communication overhead. Its ideal elapsed evaluation time is \(\lceil m/p\rceil\tau\), whereas serial execution takes \(m\tau\). The batch still consumes exactly \(m\) oracle calls. Consequently, parallel region evaluation can reduce wall-clock time by at most \(\min\{m,p\}\) for that batch, but it does not improve a Lipschitz search's worst-case evaluation bound. When evaluations have unequal durations or selection depends on earlier returns, synchronization and stale decisions can further reduce the attainable speedup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel batches can shorten wall-clock time for expensive objectives, but they do not reduce oracle-call complexity and may lose efficiency through synchronization.
assumptions_latex: The batch contains \(m\) mutually independent evaluations.
There are \(p\) identical workers and each evaluation costs \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_p=\lceil m/p\rceil\tau\) ideally, but the oracle cost remains \(m\).

notation.meaning: number of evaluations in the batch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf. Under the stated equal-duration and negligible-overhead assumptions, the batch timing and unchanged oracle count are mathematically coherent. The broader claim about worst-case Lipschitz evaluation bounds and the synchronization/staleness boundary has no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Applicability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent oracle lower bound for deterministic Lipschitz optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an algorithm evaluate an unknown \(L\)-Lipschitz function at \(N\) adaptively chosen points of \([0,1]^n\) under the \(\ell_\infty\) metric. After observing zero at every query, let \(r_N=\sup_x\min_i\|x-x_i\|_\infty\). The observations are consistent both with the zero function and with \(g(x)=-L\min_i\|x-x_i\|_\infty\), whose minimum is \(-Lr_N\). Volume covering gives \(r_N\geq(2N^{1/n})^{-1}\). Hence a sampled incumbent cannot be guaranteed within \(\varepsilon\) of the global minimum unless \(N\geq(L/(2\varepsilon))^n\), exhibiting exponential dependence on dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Black-box Lipschitz optimization on a cube generally needs exponentially many samples in dimension to guarantee a fixed global accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The oracle is deterministic and returns exact function values.
The function class contains all \(L\)-Lipschitz functions on \([0,1]^n\) under \(\ell_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\geq(L/(2\varepsilon))^n\) is necessary for the stated sampled-incumbent guarantee.

notation.meaning: covering radius of the queried points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is appropriate, and the adversarial covering-radius argument is internally plausible for exact deterministic evaluations and a sampled-incumbent guarantee. Because the exact constant, metric-specific covering argument, adaptive-information interpretation, and guarantee class have no authoritative locator, the record requires a source before acceptance.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Lipschitz Extensions
children.top_down_role: Extensions combining continuous Lipschitz structure with discrete decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Lipschitz Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz lower bounds on a finite-discrete, compact-continuous product domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=D\times C\), where \(D\) is finite and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is compact. Equip \(X\) with \(d((z,x),(z',x'))=\alpha\mathbf1_{z\ne z'}+\|x-x'\|\), where \(\alpha>0\). If \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in this metric, then a sample \((z_i,x_i)) gives the valid lower bound \(f(z,x)\geq f(z_i,x_i)-L(\alpha\mathbf1_{z\ne z_i}+\|x-x_i\|)\). Maximizing these cones over samples and minimizing over a mixed region yields a certified regional lower bound; partition search may therefore branch on discrete values and continuous subregions within one metric framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product metric turns discrete changes and continuous displacement into one Lipschitz bound, enabling certified lower bounds on mixed-variable regions.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, \(C\) is compact, and \(\alpha>0\).
\(|f(u)-f(v)|\leq Ld(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in D\times C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_i\{f(z_i,x_i)-Ld((z,x),(z_i,x_i))\}\leq f(z,x)\) on \(D\times C\).

notation.meaning: metric cost of changing a discrete assignment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the product-metric construction, and the displayed cone inequality follows from the stated Lipschitz assumption. No mixed-integer Lipschitz or partition-search source is cited, so its status as an established extension and the claimed search interpretation remain unsupported.

children.title: Multiobjective Lipschitz Search
children.top_down_role: Lipschitz search settings involving multiple competing objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiobjective Lipschitz Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise regional bounds for Lipschitz multiobjective minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):X\to\mathbb R^m\), where each component is \(L_j\)-Lipschitz. For a region \(R\) and samples \(x_i\), define \(\ell_j(R)=\max_i\{f_j(x_i)-L_j\sup_{x\in R}d(x,x_i)\}\). Then \(\ell_j(R)\leq f_j(x)\) for every \(x\in R\) and every component \(j\). If an evaluated objective vector \(y\) satisfies \(y_j\leq\ell_j(R)\) for all \(j\), with at least one strict inequality, every image in \(F(R)\) is dominated by \(y\); hence \(R\) contains no globally Pareto-optimal point and may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise Lipschitz bounds allow a region to be discarded when one evaluated objective vector dominates its entire attainable image.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is compact and \(R\subseteq X\).
Each \(f_j\) is \(L_j\)-Lipschitz and all objectives are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\preceq\ell(R)\) with one strict component implies that \(R\) contains no Pareto-optimal point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is acceptable for this leaf. Given that the evaluated vector is feasible and all objectives are minimized, the componentwise lower-bound dominance test correctly excludes Pareto-optimal points from the region. An authoritative multiobjective Lipschitz-search locator is nevertheless absent.

children.title: Discrete–Continuous Search Interface
children.top_down_role: Interaction between discrete enumeration or partitioning and continuous Lipschitz search.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete–Continuous Search Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested partition protocol for mixed discrete and continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=D\times C\), initialize one active continuous region \(C_z=C\) for each admissible \(z\in D\), or generate such assignments by discrete branching. Maintain a common priority queue of pairs \((z,R)\), each carrying a valid lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in R}f(z,x)\). Repeatedly remove a pair of minimum bound, evaluate an unevaluated point \((z,x_R)\), subdivide only its continuous region \(R\), and insert the children with updated bounds. Discard a pair only when its lower bound is no smaller than the incumbent minus the target tolerance. Return the incumbent when the global queue gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treat each discrete assignment as a family of continuous regions, rank all mixed regions by common lower bounds, and certify using the global queue gap.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and \(C\) is compact.
Every queued pair has a valid lower bound and continuous refinement is exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{UB}-\min_{(z,R)}\ell(z,R)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.

notation.meaning: discrete assignment paired with a continuous region
valid lower bound for a mixed region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the discrete-continuous interface leaf, and the global lower-bound queue gives a coherent conditional certificate when all mixed regions are covered by valid bounds. No source supports this particular nested branching protocol, pruning rule, or exhaustive-refinement interface.

children.title: Pareto Certification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of scalar optimality certificates when transferred to Pareto-set recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Certification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite regional bounds naturally certify approximate, not generally exact, Pareto coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\) be evaluated and let active regions \(R\) cover \(X\). Suppose \(\ell(R)\preceq F(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). If for every active \(R\) there exists \(s_R\in S\) satisfying \(F(s_R)\preceq\ell(R)+\varepsilon\mathbf1\), then for every \(x\in X\) some evaluated point satisfies \(F(s_R)\preceq F(x)+\varepsilon\mathbf1\); thus \(F(S)\) is an additive \(\varepsilon\)-Pareto cover. With positive-radius regions and only Lipschitz lower bounds, setting \(\varepsilon=0\) will generally fail, so exact Pareto-front certification requires additional structure or limiting refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regional lower bounds can certify an additive epsilon-Pareto cover; exact finite certification generally requires stronger structure or regions refined to zero uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized and active regions cover \(X\).
Each \(\ell(R)\) is a componentwise valid lower bound on \(F(R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in X\;\exists s\in S:\ F(s)\preceq F(x)+\varepsilon\mathbf1\), while exact certification is not generally finite.

notation.meaning: componentwise lower-bound vector for region R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container. The additive coverage implication follows from the stated componentwise regional bounds, but the broader assertion that exact finite Pareto certification generally fails under positive-radius Lipschitz bounds requires an authoritative source and a clearly specified Pareto approximation convention.
